1.B.1.6.3.description: Outer membrane porin of 319 aas ( Brunen et al. 1991 ).

1.B.1.9.2.name: Major porin of 369 aas, involved in anaerobic respiration, positively regulated by both CRP and FNR, OmpS38 or Omp35.
1.B.1.9.2.description: Major porin of 369 aas, involved in anaerobic respiration, positively regulated by both CRP and FNR, OmpS38 or Omp35 ( Gao et al. 2015 ).

1.B.10.name: The Nucleoside-specific Channel-forming Outer Membrane Porin (Tsx) Family

1.B.102.name: The Tube-forming Protein in the Mycobacterial Envelop (TiME) Family

1.B.11.name: The Outer Membrane Fimbrial Usher Porin (FUP) Family

1.B.11.3.3.name: Type γ 4 fimbrial usher, HtrE or EcpC.
1.B.11.3.3.description: Type γ 4 fimbrial usher, HtrE or EcpC. Functions with EcpD to assemble the E. coli common pilus, and extracellular fiber-like structure that plays a role in early biofilm formation and host cell recognition ( Garnett et al. 2012 ).

1.B.13.1.1.name: Alginate export porin, AEP or AlgE.
1.B.13.1.1.description: Alginate export porin, AEP or AlgE ( Rehm et al. 1994 ). A monomeric 18 stranded beta-barrel that is part of a multicomponent, two membrane, envelope-spanning complex that includes AlgK, AlgX and Alg44 ( Rehman and Rehm 2013 ).

1.B.14.1.1.name: FhuE ferric-coprogen receptor of 729 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.14.1.1.description: FhuE ferric-coprogen receptor of 729 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS. It is required for the uptake of Fe 3+ via coprogen, ferrioxamine B, and rhodotorulic acid ( Hantke 1983 ). The crystal structure of FhuE in complex with coprogen was determined, providing a structural basis to explain its selective promiscuity ( Grinter and Lithgow 2019 ). The structural data, in combination with functional analysis…

1.B.14.1.10.name: The outer membrane ferrioxamine/desferrioxamine receptor, FoxA(1) (most like TC# 1.B.14.1.4 and 9)
1.B.14.1.10.description: The outer membrane ferrioxamine/desferrioxamine receptor, FoxA(1) (most like TC# 1.B.14.1.4 and 9) ( Wei et al ., 2007 )

1.B.14.1.11.name: The outer membrane ferric-anguibactin receptor/transporter, FatA
1.B.14.1.11.description: The outer membrane ferric-anguibactin receptor/transporter, FatA ( Lopez and Crosa, 2007 )

1.B.14.1.12.name: FecA ferric-citrate receptor (PA3901) (62% identical to the E. coli FecA).
1.B.14.1.12.description: FecA ferric-citrate receptor (PA3901) ( Marshall et al. , 2009 ) (62% identical to the E. coli FecA).

1.B.14.1.13.name: CfrA ferric receptor.
1.B.14.1.13.description: CfrA ferric receptor ( Carswell et al. , 2008 ).

1.B.14.1.17.name: Ferrioxamine receptor, FoxA.
1.B.14.1.17.description: Ferrioxamine receptor, FoxA. Transports a variety of Ferrioxamine B analogues ( Kornreich-Leshem et al. 2005).

1.B.14.1.20.name: The iron-citrate receptor/transporter, FecA.
1.B.14.1.20.description: The iron-citrate receptor/transporter, FecA. TonB mediates both signaling and transport by unfolding portions of the transporter ( Mokdad et al. 2012) . The ferric citrate regulator, FecR, is translocated across the bacterial inner membrane via a unique Twin-arginine transport dependent mechanism ( Passmore et al. 2020 ).

1.B.14.1.22.name: FepA ferri-enterobactin (also Colicins B and D) receptor for the 37 aas disulfide-containing K + channel toxin, BgK.
1.B.14.1.22.description: FepA ferri-enterobactin (also Colicins B and D) receptor for the 37 aas disulfide-containing K + channel toxin, BgK ( Braud et al. , 2004 ). Functions by a "ball and chain" mechanism; The transport process involves expulsion of the N-terminal globular domain from the C-terminal beta-barrel ( Ma et al. 2007 ). Conformational rearrangements occur in the N-terminus of FepA during FeEnt transport…

1.B.14.1.25.name: Nickel uptake receptor/channel of 724 aas.
1.B.14.1.25.description: Nickel uptake receptor/channel of 724 aas ( Benoit et al. 2013 ).

1.B.14.1.26.name: Iron siderophore (ferripyoverdine) receptor and importer, FpvA of 808 aas.
1.B.14.1.26.description: Iron siderophore (ferripyoverdine) receptor and importer, FpvA of 808 aas ( Ye et al. 2014 ). The crystal structure of FpvA has been solved at 3.6 Å resolution. It is folded in two domains: a transmembrane 22-stranded beta-barrel domain occluded by an N-terminal domain containing a mixed four-stranded beta-sheet (the plug). The beta-strands of the barrel are connected by long extracellular loops…

1.B.14.1.29.name: Iron-deficiency-induced (2x) iron siderophore uptake outer membrane receptor, FhuA, of 828 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.14.1.29.description: Iron-deficiency-induced (2x) iron siderophore uptake outer membrane receptor, FhuA, of 828 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS ( Qiu et al. 2018 ).

1.B.14.1.3.name: Ferric enterobactin (also ferricorynebactin) receptor, IroN The microbial metabolite, Enterobactin, impairs mitochondrial respiration and alleviates…
1.B.14.1.3.description: Ferric enterobactin (also ferricorynebactin) receptor, IroN The microbial metabolite, Enterobactin, impairs mitochondrial respiration and alleviates colitis in humans ( Kushwaha et al. 2026 ).

1.B.14.1.30.name: Outer membrand iron siderophore uptake receptor of 853 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS, Slr1490.
1.B.14.1.30.description: Outer membrand iron siderophore uptake receptor of 853 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS, Slr1490.

1.B.14.1.31.name: Outer membrane porin, PiuA, of 753 aas.
1.B.14.1.31.description: Outer membrane porin, PiuA, of 753 aas. A deficiency of this iron transporter, PiuA in P. aeruginosa , caused 16-fold increases in cefiderocol resistance, suggesting that it contribute to the permeation of cefiderocol into the cell ( Ito et al. 2018 ).

1.B.14.1.32.name: Catechol iron-siderophore uptake system, IrgA, an iron-regulated outer membrane virulence protein , of 652 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.14.1.32.description: Catechol iron-siderophore uptake system, IrgA, an iron-regulated outer membrane virulence protein , of 652 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS ( Wyckoff et al. 2015 ). It is involved in the initial step of iron uptake by binding ferric vibriobactin, an iron chelatin siderophore that allows V. cholerae to extract iron from the environment and takes up linear enterobactin derivatives ( Wyckoff et al. 2015 ).

1.B.14.1.4.name: CirA Fe 3+ -catecholate receptor.
1.B.14.1.4.description: CirA Fe 3+ -catecholate receptor. Serves as the receptor for the TonB- and proton-dependent uptake of the E. coli bacteriocin, Microcin L (MccL) ( Morin et al. , 2011 ). CirA is also the translocator for colicin Ia ( Jakes and Finkelstein, 2010 ). Plays roles in cefiderocol and ceftazidime resistance ( Ito et al. 2018 ). Genotypic evolution of Klebsiella pneumoniae sequence type 512 during…

1.B.14.1.6.name: Ferripyoverdine/pyocin S3 receptor, FpvA
1.B.14.1.6.description: Ferripyoverdine/pyocin S3 receptor, FpvA ( Adams et al ., 2006 ; Nader et al ., 2007 ; Schalk et al. , 2009 ; Nader et al. , 2011 )

1.B.14.1.8.name: The Ferripyochelin receptor, FptA.
1.B.14.1.8.description: The Ferripyochelin receptor, FptA ( Michel et al ., 2007 ). In addition to Fe 3+ , FptA takes up Co 2+ , Ga 3+ , and Ni 2+ at low rates ( Braud et al. , 2009 ). The high resolution 3-d structure of FptA (2.0 Å) bound to iron-pyochelin has been solved ( Cobessi et al. 2005 ). The pyochelin molecule provides atetra-dentate coordination of iron. The structure is typical of the TonB-dependent…

1.B.14.1.9.name: Ferric-catecholate siderophore (dihydroxybenzoylserine, dihydroxybenzoate) uptake receptor, Fiu or YbiL.
1.B.14.1.9.description: Ferric-catecholate siderophore (dihydroxybenzoylserine, dihydroxybenzoate) uptake receptor, Fiu or YbiL ( Hantke, 1990 ; Curtis et al ., 1988 ). Plays roles in cefiderocol and ceftazidime resistance ( Ito et al. 2018 ). It can also transport catechol-substituted cephalosporins and is a receptor for microcins M, H47 and E492 ( Patzer et al. 2003 ; Destoumieux-Garzón et al. 2006 ).

1.B.14.10.1.name: Heme/hemoglobin receptor, HmuR (also binds the Cu 2+ , Zn 2+ and Fe 2+ derivatives of protoporphyrin IX).
1.B.14.10.1.description: Heme/hemoglobin receptor, HmuR (also binds the Cu 2+ , Zn 2+ and Fe 2+ derivatives of protoporphyrin IX). Functions with the O.M. heme binding lipoprotein, HmuY (AAQ66587; Olczak et al ., 2007 ).

1.B.14.10.6.name: Cobalt cation concentration sensitive Btu-like system, Btu1, of 698 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.14.10.6.description: Cobalt cation concentration sensitive Btu-like system, Btu1, of 698 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS. It facilitates cobalamin uptake in Anabaena sp. PCC 7120 ( Graf et al. 2024 ). The regulation by cobalt and cobalamin as well as their uptakes are described for Anabaena sp. PCC 7120, a model filamentous heterocyst-forming cyanobacterium. Anabaena contains at least three cobalamin riboswitches in its…

1.B.14.12.1.name: The TonB-dependent maltooligosaccharide OM receptor/porin, MalA.
1.B.14.12.1.description: The TonB-dependent maltooligosaccharide OM receptor/porin, MalA ( Lohmiller et al ., 2008 ).

1.B.14.12.2.name: The N-acetyl glucosamine/chitin oligosaccharide OM receptor porin, NagA.
1.B.14.12.2.description: The N-acetyl glucosamine/chitin oligosaccharide OM receptor porin, NagA ( Eisenbeis et al ., 2008 ).

1.B.14.16.10.name: Putative LPS exporter receptor, OtuG.
1.B.14.16.10.description: Putative LPS exporter receptor, OtuG. It's gene is in a cluster with several LPS biosynthetic enzymes.

1.B.14.16.11.name: OMR of 698 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS, GlfD or YmcA.
1.B.14.16.11.description: OMR of 698 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS, GlfD or YmcA. Probably involved in capsular polysaccharide export ( Peleg et al. 2005 ).

1.B.14.16.4.name: DUF940 homologue of 940 aas, one N-terminal signal sequence and 32 putative TM β-strands.
1.B.14.16.4.description: DUF940 homologue of 940 aas, one N-terminal signal sequence and 32 putative TM β-strands.

1.B.14.16.8.name: Putative polysaccharide/glycolipid/glycoprotein export receptor of 736 aas and 30 predicted β-strands, WbfB.
1.B.14.16.8.description: Putative polysaccharide/glycolipid/glycoprotein export receptor of 736 aas and 30 predicted β-strands, WbfB. The gene encoding this protein is in a cluster with UDP-N-acetyl D-quinovosamine -4 epimerase.

1.B.14.16.9.name: Putative lipopolysaccharide export receptor, WbfB.
1.B.14.16.9.description: Putative lipopolysaccharide export receptor, WbfB. It is encoded in a gene cluster with LPS biosynthetic genes.

1.B.14.19.1.name: Putative TonB-dpenedent receptor of 790 aas, YddB.
1.B.14.19.1.description: Putative TonB-dpenedent receptor of 790 aas, YddB. It is encoded by a gene adjacent to the YddA-encoding gene (TC# 3.A.1.203.11). YddA is a probable fatty acid exporter. the yddB gene is adjacent to a gene encoding a putative Zn 2+ protease, PqqL.

1.B.14.2.15.name: Uncharacterized outer membrane receptor, probably for iron transport.
1.B.14.2.15.description: Uncharacterized outer membrane receptor, probably for iron transport.

1.B.14.2.17.name: The iron-catechol siderophore uptake/receptor, VctA, of 659 aas.
1.B.14.2.17.description: The iron-catechol siderophore uptake/receptor, VctA, of 659 aas. Linear enterobactin derivatives are substrates, but it also transports the synthetic siderophore MECAM [1,3,5-N,N',N″-tris-(2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl)-triaminomethylbenzene] ( Wyckoff et al. 2015 ).

1.B.14.2.3.name: HpuAB hemoglobin-haptoglobin receptor; porphyrin transporter (HpuA=lipoprotein; HpuB=OMR porin).
1.B.14.2.3.description: HpuAB hemoglobin-haptoglobin receptor; porphyrin transporter (HpuA=lipoprotein; HpuB=OMR porin). Surface exposed loops in the gonococcal HpuB transporter are important for hemoglobin binding and utilization ( Awate et al. 2023 ).

1.B.14.2.7.name: Hemin (Heme)-binding receptor, ShmR (also transports the toxic heme analog, gallium protoporphyrin).
1.B.14.2.7.description: Hemin (Heme)-binding receptor, ShmR (also transports the toxic heme analog, gallium protoporphyrin) ( Amarelle et al. , 2008 ).

1.B.14.2.8.name: The heme-iron (from hemin and hemoglobin) utilization receptor, BhuR.
1.B.14.2.8.description: The heme-iron (from hemin and hemoglobin) utilization receptor, BhuR ( Brickman et al. , 2006 ; Vanderpool and Armstrong, 2004 ).

1.B.14.3.1.name: BtuB cobalamin receptor (also transports phage C1 DNA across the outer membrane).
1.B.14.3.1.description: BtuB cobalamin receptor (also transports phage C1 DNA across the outer membrane). Two Ca 2+ binding sites in BtuB mediate cobalamine binding ( Cadieux et al ., 2007 ). Cobalamine uptake into the periplasm is reversible, but efflux is pmf-independent ( Cadieux et al ., 2007 ). The 3-d structure is available (PDB#1NQE). The Ton box and the extracellular substrate binding site are allosterically…

1.B.14.4.1.name: Cu 2+ -transporting, Cu 2+ -regulated outer membrane protein C, OprC.
1.B.14.4.1.description: Cu 2+ -transporting, Cu 2+ -regulated outer membrane protein C, OprC ( Yoneyama and Nakae 1996 ). OprC impairs host defense by increasing the quorum-sensing-mediated virulence of P. aeruginosa ( Gao et al. 2020 ).

1.B.14.5.2.name: The heme receptor HxuC (PA1302) serves as a pyocin M4 (Colicin M-type; PaeM4) target at the cellular surface.
1.B.14.5.2.description: The heme receptor HxuC (PA1302) serves as a pyocin M4 (Colicin M-type; PaeM4) target at the cellular surface.

1.B.14.6.15.name: TonB-dependent collagenase (proteinase) of 1047 aas.
1.B.14.6.15.description: TonB-dependent collagenase (proteinase) of 1047 aas ( Bhattacharya et al. 2017 ). The primary pathogen of the Great Barrier Reef sponge, Rhopaloeides odorabile , identified as a unique strain (NW4327) of Pseudoalteromonas agarivorans . It produces collagenases which degrade R. odorabile skeletal fibers.

1.B.14.6.5.name: TonB-dependent outer membrane receptor of 792 aas.
1.B.14.6.5.description: TonB-dependent outer membrane receptor of 792 aas.

1.B.14.8.2.name: The iron (Fe 3+ ) · pyridine-2,6-bis(thiocarboxylic acid) (PDTC) receptor, PdtK.
1.B.14.8.2.description: The iron (Fe 3+ ) · pyridine-2,6-bis(thiocarboxylic acid) (PDTC) receptor, PdtK. Functions with the MFS carrier, PdtE (TC #2.A.1.55.1) ( Leach and Lewis, 2006 ).

1.B.14.8.3.name: Vibriobactin receptor, VuiA or VuuA of 687 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.14.8.3.description: Vibriobactin receptor, VuiA or VuuA of 687 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS. There is conserved, global coordinate iron regulation in V. cholerae by the Fur transcription factor, responsive to iron ( Butterton et al. 1992 ). V. cholerae synthesizes and uses the catechol siderophore vibriobactin and also uses siderophores secreted by other species, including enterobactin produced by E. coli ( Wyckoff et…

1.B.14.8.4.name: The thiamine receptor (SO2715) (energized by TonB/ExbBD)
1.B.14.8.4.description: The thiamine receptor (SO2715) (energized by TonB/ExbBD) ( Rodionov et al. 2002 )

1.B.14.9.3.name: The ferric ferrichrome/aerobactin receptor/porin, IutA
1.B.14.9.3.description: The ferric ferrichrome/aerobactin receptor/porin, IutA ( Forman et al ., 2007 )

1.B.14.9.5.name: TonB-dependent receptor of 700 aas, YncD, a probable iron transporter/receptor in the outer membrane.
1.B.14.9.5.description: TonB-dependent receptor of 700 aas, YncD, a probable iron transporter/receptor in the outer membrane. Deletion of the orthologous yncD genes in Salmonella strains leads to attenuated strains, potentially useful for vaccine development ( Xiong et al. 2012 ; Xiong et al. 2015). Its synthesis is depressed by inclusion of high glucose concentrations in the medium ( Yang et al. 2011 ). YncD is a…

1.B.14.9.6.name: SchT (IutA) is capable of using dihydroxamate xenosiderophores, either ferric schizokinen (FeSK) or a siderophore of the filamentous cyanobacterium…
1.B.14.9.6.description: SchT (IutA) is capable of using dihydroxamate xenosiderophores, either ferric schizokinen (FeSK) or a siderophore of the filamentous cyanobacterium Anabaena variabilis ATCC 29413 (SAV), as the sole source of iron in a TonB-dependent manner ( Obando S et al. 2018 ). Functions with the ABC uptake system having the TC# 3.A.1.14.24.

1.B.16.name: The Short Chain Amide and Urea Porin (SAP) Family

1.B.17.1.3.name: The OMF, EexF (functions with ABC exporter, EexD (TC# 3.A.1.110.10) and MFP EexE (TC# 8.A.1.3.3)).
1.B.17.1.3.description: The OMF, EexF (functions with ABC exporter, EexD (TC# 3.A.1.110.10) and MFP EexE (TC# 8.A.1.3.3)) ( Gimmestad et al ., 2006 ).

1.B.17.1.4.name: TolC of Sinorhizobium meliloti (affects secretion of proteins, polysaccharide, and multiple drugs)
1.B.17.1.4.description: TolC of Sinorhizobium meliloti (affects secretion of proteins, polysaccharide, and multiple drugs ( Cosme et al ., 2008 ))

1.B.17.2.10.name: Putative ABC-type glycolipid export outer membrane factor, HgdD, of 483 aas.
1.B.17.2.10.description: Putative ABC-type glycolipid export outer membrane factor, HgdD, of 483 aas (Hahn et al. , 2012).

1.B.17.2.2.name: CzcC outer membrane exporter of Co 2+ , Cd 2+ , Zn 2+.
1.B.17.2.2.description: CzcC outer membrane exporter of Co 2+ , Cd 2+ , Zn 2+ . Functions with CzcAB (2.A.6.1.2).

1.B.17.3.11.name: TolC-like outer membrane factor protein, TdeA of 457 aas, required for leukotoxin and drug export.
1.B.17.3.11.description: TolC-like outer membrane factor protein, TdeA of 457 aas, required for leukotoxin and drug export ( Crosby and Kachlany 2007 ). Functions with the MFP, LtxD (TC# 8.A.1.3.4) and the ABC exporter (TC# 3.A.1.109.8).

1.B.17.3.13.name: Multidrug resistance protein in the Outer Membrane Factor (OMF) Family of 490 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.17.3.13.description: Multidrug resistance protein in the Outer Membrane Factor (OMF) Family of 490 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS ( Hasan et al. 2024 ).

1.B.17.3.2.name: FusA outer membrane exporter of fusaric acid
1.B.17.3.2.description: FusA outer membrane exporter of fusaric acid

1.B.17.3.4.name: SilC outer membrane exporter of silver ion, Ag +
1.B.17.3.4.description: SilC outer membrane exporter of silver ion, Ag +

1.B.17.3.5.name: CusC outer membrane exporter of copper ion, Cu + , and silver ion Ag +.
1.B.17.3.5.description: CusC outer membrane exporter of copper ion, Cu + , and silver ion Ag +. The crystal structure of CusC is known ( Lei et al. 2013 ) providing evidnce concerning the folding mechanism giving rise to the channel.

1.B.17.3.7.name: HI1462 outer membrane, low conductance, anion-selective exporter (selectivity is due to an arginine residue at the tunnel entrance).
1.B.17.3.7.description: HI1462 outer membrane, low conductance, anion-selective exporter (selectivity is due to an arginine residue at the tunnel entrance). ( Polleichtner and Anderson, 2006 )

1.B.17.3.8.name: Chromosomal NodTch (orthologous to 1.B.17.3.1) (478 aas) required for cell survival.
1.B.17.3.8.description: Chromosomal NodTch (orthologous to 1.B.17.3.1) (478 aas) required for cell survival ( Hernandez-Mendoza et al ., 2007 ).

1.B.18.name: The Outer Membrane Auxiliary (OMA) Protein Family

1.B.18.1.2.name: OMA protein component of an ABC-type group 2 capsular polysaccharide (polysialic acid) export system (outer membrane porin constituent)
1.B.18.1.2.description: OMA protein component of an ABC-type group 2 capsular polysaccharide (polysialic acid) export system (outer membrane porin constituent)

1.B.18.2.3.name: Capsular polysialate exporter component, CtrA.
1.B.18.2.3.description: Capsular polysialate exporter component, CtrA. OMA of 3.A.1.101.3 (functions with 3.A.1.101.3 (ABC) and 8.B.4.2.1 (MPA2)) ( Larue et al. , 2011 )

1.B.18.3.1.name: OMA component of the group 1 K30 capsular polysaccharide, colanic acid, export system, Wza (outer membrane porin constituent).
1.B.18.3.1.description: OMA component of the group 1 K30 capsular polysaccharide, colanic acid, export system, Wza ( Reid and Whitfield, 2005 ) (outer membrane porin constituent). The 3-d structure of the Wza/Wzc complex has been solved by Collins et al. (2007) . It spans the periplasm, comprising a central constituent for complex formation. The x-ray structure shows an integral outer membrane transmembrane α-helical…

1.B.18.3.8.name: Outer membrane auxillary lipoprotein of 698 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS, GlfD or YmcA.
1.B.18.3.8.description: Outer membrane auxillary lipoprotein of 698 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS, GlfD or YmcA. Probably involved in capsular polysaccharide export ( Peleg et al. 2005 ; Cuthbertson et al. 2009 ; Nadler et al. 2012 ).

1.B.18.3.9.name: Outer membrane polysaccharide biosynthesis/export protein, Opx, EpsY or MXAN_7417 of 219 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.18.3.9.description: Outer membrane polysaccharide biosynthesis/export protein, Opx, EpsY or MXAN_7417 of 219 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS. The gene encoding this protein is adjacent to EpsZ (MXAN_7415; TC# 9.B.18.1.6), an exopolysaccharide biosynthetic protein, and Wzx (MXAN_7416; TC# 2.A.66.12.12), a polysaccharide cytoplasmic membrane flippase ( Pérez-Burgos et al. 2020 ).

1.B.19.1.1.name: Cation-selective, glucose-inducible glucose-transporting porin (also transports glycerol, mannitol, fructose, maltose, pentoses, etc.).
1.B.19.1.1.description: Cation-selective, glucose-inducible glucose-transporting porin (also transports glycerol, mannitol, fructose, maltose, pentoses, etc.) ( Adewoye and Worobec 1999 ).

1.B.19.1.3.name: Carbohydrate-selective porin OprB.
1.B.19.1.3.description: Carbohydrate-selective porin OprB ( Shrivastava et al. , 2011 ). The high resolution 3-d structure reveals a 16 β-TMS barrel with a constriction explaining the preference of this porin for monosaccharides over disaccharides ( van den Berg 2012 ).

1.B.19.1.9.name: Porin of 425 aas, OprB, required for virulence and biofilm formation.
1.B.19.1.9.description: Porin of 425 aas, OprB, required for virulence and biofilm formation ( Ficarra et al. 2016 ). It is a sugar-selective porin ( Bae et al. 2018 ).

1.B.20.1.8.name: Hemolysin activator protein, ExlB of 570 aas.
1.B.20.1.8.description: Hemolysin activator protein, ExlB of 570 aas. Exports the exotoxin, ExlA (TC# 1.C.73.1.1) ( Elsen et al. 2014 ; Basso et al. 2017 ).

1.B.20.2.2.name: The ShlB/FhaC/HecB family hemolysin secretion/activation protein of 555 aas.
1.B.20.2.2.description: The ShlB/FhaC/HecB family hemolysin secretion/activation protein of 555 aas.

1.B.20.3.7.name: Uncharacterized protein of 455 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.
1.B.20.3.7.description: Uncharacterized protein of 455 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS.

1.B.22.name: The Outer Bacterial Membrane Secretin (Secretin) Family

1.B.22.1.1.name: PulD protein secretin.
1.B.22.1.1.description: PulD protein secretin. Involved in protein secretion via the Type II MTB system (TC# 3.A.15). PulD allows the efflux of small fluorescent molecules with a permeation cutoff similar to that of general porins and is constitutively open ( Disconzi et al. 2014 ).

1.B.22.1.3.name: The dodecameric secretin, GspD of 650 aas.
1.B.22.1.3.description: The dodecameric secretin, GspD of 650 aas. The 3-d structure is known (PDB 5WQ8) ( Korotkov et al. 2013 ). It reveals a double β-barrel channel with about 60 β-strands in each barrel ( Yan et al. 2017 ).

1.B.22.4.2.name: HofQ, may facilitate double stranded DNA uptake in E. coli.
1.B.22.4.2.description: HofQ, may facilitate double stranded DNA uptake in E. coli ( Sun et al. , 2009 ).

1.B.22.4.3.name: HofQ competence protein, the outer membrane DNA translocase.

2.A.1.14.14.description: Probable D-galactarate (glucarate?):H + symporter, GarP or YhaU. May also function as a glucarate:glycerate antiporter ( Moraes and Reithmeier 2012 ) and a glucose transporter. This sequence is incomplete.

2.A.1.14.2.name: Hexuronate (glucuronate; galacturonate) porter, ExuT.
2.A.1.14.2.description: Hexuronate (glucuronate; galacturonate) porter, ExuT ( Nemoz et al. 1976 ). It also transports D-glucose ( Kim et al. 2020 ).

2.A.1.14.25.name: The putative D-mannuronate porter, AlgT.
2.A.1.14.25.description: The putative D-mannuronate porter, AlgT ( Rodionov et al. , 2010 ).

2.A.1.14.3.name: Putative tartrate porter, TtuB or TUB3, of 449 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.14.3.description: Putative tartrate porter, TtuB or TUB3, of 449 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.14.33.name: L-galactonate transporter, YjjL or DgoT of 460 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.14.33.description: L-galactonate transporter, YjjL or DgoT of 460 aas and 12 TMSs. The D-galactonate transporter DgoT has been solved at atomic resolution ( Dmitrieva et al. 2024 ). Protonation of D46 and E133 precedes galactonate binding, and substrate binding induces closure of the extracellular gate, with the conserved R47 coupling substrate binding to transmembrane helix movement. After isomerization to an…

2.A.1.14.40.name: Glucarate transporter, GudP.
2.A.1.14.40.description: Glucarate transporter, GudP. Encoded in an operon with GudD, a glucarate dehydratase ( Moraes and Reithmeier 2012 ).

2.A.1.15.16.name: Aromatic/benzoate uptake transporter of 442 aas and 12 TMSs, BenK.
2.A.1.15.16.description: Aromatic/benzoate uptake transporter of 442 aas and 12 TMSs, BenK ( Choudhary et al. 2017 ).

2.A.1.15.2.name: MhpT.
2.A.1.15.2.description: MhpT. A specific 3-(3-hydroxyphenyl)propionate (3HPP) transporter; vital for E. coli K-12 W3110 to grow on this substrate. Transports 3HPP but not benzoate, 3-hydroxybenzoate or gentisate ( Xu et al. 2013 ). May also export arabinose but not xylose ( Koita and Rao 2012 ).

2.A.1.15.7.name: Aromatic compound (benzoate) uptake transporter of 450 aas.
2.A.1.15.7.description: Aromatic compound (benzoate) uptake transporter of 450 aas ( Clark et al. 2002 ).

2.A.1.15.9.name: Probable 4-methylmuconolactone transporter, MmlH
2.A.1.15.9.description: Probable 4-methylmuconolactone transporter, MmlH ( Erb et al ., 1998 )

2.A.1.17.1.name: Cyanate transport system, CynT.
2.A.1.17.1.description: Cyanate transport system, CynT. Encoded with cyanate aminohydrolase, CynS, and carbonic anhydrase, CynX ( Anderson et al. 1990; Moraes and Reithmeier 2012 ).

2.A.1.17.3.name: Inner membrane transport protein, NimT or YeaN of 393 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.17.3.description: Inner membrane transport protein, NimT or YeaN of 393 aas and 12 TMSs. It exports 2-nitroimidazole from the cytoplasm, confering resistance to this anitbiotic, and transcription of this gene as well as NimO, within the same operon, is regulated by the repressor, NimR (YeaM) ( Ogasawara et al. 2015 ).

2.A.1.2.102.name: TetA class C (TetA(C)) of 396 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.102.description: TetA class C (TetA(C)) of 396 aas and 12 TMSs. The TetA(C) of the transposon, Tn10, not only exports tetracycline by a proton antiport mechanism, it also increases susceptibility to cadmium, fusaric acid , bleomycin and several classes of cationic aminoglycoside antibiotics ( Griffith et al. 1995 ). For this reason, it has been used to generate dual counter selection procedures ( Li et al. 2013…

2.A.1.2.103.name: Tetracycline:H + class D, (TetA(D)) antiporter of 286 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.103.description: Tetracycline:H + class D, (TetA(D)) antiporter of 286 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.2.107.name: MFS porter of 399 aas and 12 TMSs, HepP, involved in the uptake of glycoside(s), with a specific physiological role in production of heterocyst…
2.A.1.2.107.description: MFS porter of 399 aas and 12 TMSs, HepP, involved in the uptake of glycoside(s), with a specific physiological role in production of heterocyst exopolysaccharide, HEP ( López-Igual et al. 2012 ).

2.A.1.2.109.name: MFS porter of 414 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.109.description: MFS porter of 414 aas and 12 TMSs. It has been suggested that it could be a citrate efflux porter ( Braakman et al. 2017 ).

2.A.1.2.110.name: Florfenicol-chloramphenicol resistance drug exporter, FloR of 404 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.110.description: Florfenicol-chloramphenicol resistance drug exporter, FloR of 404 aas and 12 TMSs ( Braibant et al. 2005 ). This system in V. cholerae (98.8% identical) exports chlorampenicol ( Saha et al. 2024 ).

2.A.1.2.116.name: MDR efflux pump, Bcr/CflA, of 411 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.116.description: MDR efflux pump, Bcr/CflA, of 411 aas and 12 TMSs. Confer's chloramphenicol resistance ( Yang et al. 2019 ).

2.A.1.2.122.name: MfsC (Smlt0549), a probable diamide exporter of 379 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.1.2.122.description: MfsC (Smlt0549), a probable diamide exporter of 379 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement. It is encoded within the mfsBC operon controlled by the DitR TetR-like transcript factor which binds diamide to displace the repressing factor from the DNA. MfsB (BeFL18) may be a sugar uptake porter ( Boonyakanog et al. 2022 ).

2.A.1.2.15.name: Arabinose (but not xylose) and isopropyl β-D-thio-galactopyranoside:H + antiporter, YdeA.
2.A.1.2.15.description: Arabinose (but not xylose) and isopropyl β-D-thio-galactopyranoside:H + antiporter, YdeA ( Koita and Rao 2012 ). Overexpression of the gene for YdeA allows export of Lacto- N -triose (LNT II) and lacto- N -tetraose (LNT), human milk oligosaccharides ( Sugita and Koketsu 2022 ).

2.A.1.2.18.name: Lactose and melibiose (>>IPTG) efflux pump, SotB
2.A.1.2.18.description: Lactose and melibiose (>>IPTG) efflux pump, SotB

Can function as a Na + (K + )/H + antiporter ( Lewinson and Bibi 2001 ; Higgins, 2007 ). Is…

2.A.1.2.20.name: Broad specificity MDR efflux pump, MdtG (YceE) (under SoxSR control).
2.A.1.2.20.description: Broad specificity MDR efflux pump, MdtG (YceE) (under SoxSR control) ( Fàbrega et al. , 2010 ). Confer resistance to fosfomycin, fluoroquinolone and many other drugs ( Nishino and Yamaguchi 2001 ). It may also export ectoine and hydroxyectoine ( Czech et al. 2022 ). Pyoverdine-antibiotic combination treatment enhances MDR resistance. Its efficacy and effects on resistance evolution in Escherichia…

2.A.1.2.25.name: The purine base/nucleoside (nucleosides: inosine, adenosine and guanosine; bases: hypoxanthine, adenine, guanine, 2-fluoroadenine) efflux pump, YdhL…
2.A.1.2.25.description: The purine base/nucleoside (nucleosides: inosine, adenosine and guanosine; bases: hypoxanthine, adenine, guanine, 2-fluoroadenine) efflux pump, YdhL (PbuE) ( Johansen et al ., 2003 ; Nygaard and Saxild, 2005 ; Zakataeva et al ., 2007; Sheremet et al. 2011 Sheremet et al. 2011 ).

2.A.1.2.26.description: The purine ribonucleoside (inosine, adenosine, guanosine, 6-mercaptopurine ribonucleoside) efflux pump (H + antiporter), NepI (YicM) ( Gronskiy et al ., 2005 ; Sheremet et al. 2011 )

2.A.1.2.3.name: Chloramphenicol:H + antiporter, CmlA; Cmr; MdfA.
2.A.1.2.3.description: Chloramphenicol:H + antiporter, CmlA; Cmr; MdfA. Multidrug exporter that also catalyzes efflux of arabinose (but not xylose) and isopropyl β-thiogalactoside ( Koita and Rao 2012 ).

2.A.1.2.38.description: Tetracycline-specific exporter, TetA39 (most like 2.A.1.2.4) ( Thompson et al ., 2007 ).

2.A.1.2.39.description: Tetracycline-specific exporter, TetA41 (most like 2.A.1.2.4) ( Thompson et al ., 2007 ).

2.A.1.2.41.description: The tetracycline resistance determinant, TetA42 from a deep terrestrial subsurface bacterium ( Brown et al. , 2008 ).

2.A.1.2.42.name: The multidrug efflux pump, EmrD-3 (exports ethidium, linezolid, tetraphenylphosphonium chloride, rifampin, erythromycin, minocycline, trimethoprim…
2.A.1.2.42.description: The multidrug efflux pump, EmrD-3 (exports ethidium, linezolid, tetraphenylphosphonium chloride, rifampin, erythromycin, minocycline, trimethoprim, chloramphenicol, and rhodamine) ( Smith et al. , 2009 ).

2.A.1.2.51.name: Chloramphenicol resistance pump, CraA (43% identical to MdfA of E. coli ).
2.A.1.2.51.description: Chloramphenicol resistance pump, CraA (43% identical to MdfA of E. coli ) ( Roca et al. , 2009 ). It is a broad specificity transporter exporting chloramphenicol, thiamphenicol, florfenicol, ethidium, dequalinium, chlorhexidine, benzalkonium, mitomycin C and TPP + . Glu-38 is essential for activity ( Foong et al. 2019 ).

2.A.1.2.55.name: Peptide exporter (Ala-Gln and Ala-branched chain amino and dipeptides).
2.A.1.2.55.description: Peptide exporter (Ala-Gln and Ala-branched chain amino and dipeptides) ( Hayashi et al. , 2010 ). May also export arabinose (but not xylose) and function as an MDR pump ( Koita and Rao 2012 ).

2.A.1.2.60.name: YajR of 454 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.60.description: YajR of 454 aas and 12 TMSs. The 3-D structure in the outward-facing conformation is available at 3.15Å resolution, and the cytoplasmic C-terminal YAM domain has been solved to 1.07Å resolution. This 65 aa YAM domain is thought to control the conformational states of the protein ( Jiang et al. 2013 ; Jiang et al. 2014 ).

2.A.1.2.62.name: Putative MDR pump, YdhC or PunC.
2.A.1.2.62.description: Putative MDR pump, YdhC or PunC. It has been reporte to export arabinose but not xylose ( Koita and Rao 2012 ). However, it also takes up adenosine, adenine, deoxyadenosine, and other purine nucleosides and nucleobases such as inosine and guanosine as sole nitrogen sources. It also takes up various sulfonamides such as sulfathiazole, sulfadiazine and sulfamethoxazole. Expression of the punC gene…

2.A.1.2.68.name: Tetracycline resistance protein, class B (TetA(B)) (Metal-tetracycline/H + antiporter).
2.A.1.2.68.description: Tetracycline resistance protein, class B (TetA(B)) (Metal-tetracycline/H + antiporter). Mutants defective in either transport or tetracycline binding have been isolated ( Wright and Tate 2015 ). Several amino acid substitutions (i.e., D190C, E192C and S201C) alter the specificity of the porter so that it prefers deoxycycline (3x) and minochcline (6x) over tetracycline ( Sapunaric and Levy 2005 ).

2.A.1.2.7.name: Bicyclomycin, sulfathiazole, tetracycline, fosfomycin, acriflavin, etc.):H + antiporter.
2.A.1.2.7.description: Bicyclomycin, sulfathiazole, tetracycline, fosfomycin, acriflavin, etc.):H + antiporter ( Nishino and Yamaguchi 2001 ). Also exports L-cysteine ( Yamada et al. , 2006 ).

2.A.1.2.8.description: (Spermidine; fluoroquinolones, acriflavin, chloramphenicol, ethidium bromide, etc.):H + antiporter ( Woolridge et al. 1997 ).

2.A.1.2.81.description: Uncharacterized MFS permease; encoded by a gene adjacent to one encoding a peroxiredoxin (an electron donor and antioxidant; Hanschmann et al. 2013 ).

2.A.1.2.9.name: (Hydrophobic uncoupler e.g., CCCP, benzalkonium, SDS and other drugs):H + antiporter, EmrD.
2.A.1.2.9.description: (Hydrophobic uncoupler e.g., CCCP, benzalkonium, SDS and other drugs):H + antiporter, EmrD ( Nishino and Yamaguchi 2001 ). The 3-d structure (3.5 Å resolution) has been determined ( Yin et al. , 2006) . conformational dynamics studies have revealed details of the transport pathway and some motions of EmrD at an atomic level ( Baker et al. 2012 ). Probably exports arabinose but not xylose ( Koita…

2.A.1.2.97.name: Bcr/CflA family drug exporter, MSMEG_2991 of 428 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.97.description: Bcr/CflA family drug exporter, MSMEG_2991 of 428 aas and 12 TMSs. A pmf-dependent multidrug efflux pump that expels diverse groups of antibiotics including ciprofloxacin. May also be involved in biofilm enhancement ( Bansal et al. 2016 ).

2.A.1.2.98.name: Uncharacterized MFS transporter of 427 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.1.2.98.description: Uncharacterized MFS transporter of 427 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.1.20.1.name: Sugar efflux transporter A, SetA.
2.A.1.20.1.description: Sugar efflux transporter A, SetA. Exports lactose, glucose, aromatic glucosides and galactosides, cellobiose, maltose, α-methylglucoside and isopropyl β-thiogalactosides (IPTG); amino-glycosides, streptomycin and kanamycin are weakly expelled ( Liu et al. 1999 ). Regulated by SgrR (a transcriptional regulator of sgrS ) and SgrS (a small RNA that represses trascription of setA ). These two…

2.A.1.20.2.name: Sugar efflux system, SetB, for lactose and glucose, but not IPTG or galactose.
2.A.1.20.2.description: Sugar efflux system, SetB, for lactose and glucose, but not IPTG or galactose ( Liu et al. 1999 ). Overexpression of the gene for SetB allows export of Lacto- N -triose (LNT II) and lacto- N -tetraose (LNT), human milk oligosaccharides ( Sugita and Koketsu 2022 ).

2.A.1.20.3.name: Arabinose (but not xylose) exporter, SetC.

2.A.1.21.1.description: The macrolide (erythromycin; oleandomycin; azithromycin; telithromycin) efflux pump, MefA, of 405 aas and 12 TMSs ( Cantón et al. 2005 ; Bley et al. 2011 ). However, the data presented seem inconsistent with this suggestion. The two genes encoding these two…

2.A.1.21.22.name: Macrolide efflux pump, MefE (Mef; MefA) of 405 aas.
2.A.1.21.22.description: Macrolide efflux pump, MefE (Mef; MefA) of 405 aas. Induced by erythromycin and the antimicrobial peptide, LL-37 ( Zähner et al. 2010 ). May act in conjunction with Mel (Q93QE4), an ABC-type ATPase that is encoded in the same operon with the mefA gene ( Ambrose et al. 2005 ).

2.A.1.27.1.description: The phenylpropionate porter, HcaT (YfhS) ( Díaz et al. 1998 ).

2.A.1.3.26.description: Novobiocin/deoxycholate exporting MDR efflux pump, MdtD or YegB ( Baranova and Nikaido, 2002 ). Also exports arabinose but not xylose ( Koita and Rao 2012 ). Regulated by the transcription factor, BaeR ( Nagakubo et al. 2002 ).

2.A.1.3.37.description: The uridine/deoxyuridine/5-fluorouridine uptake transporter, UriP (llmg_0856) (480aas; 14TMSs) ( Martinussen et al. , 2010 )

2.A.1.3.62.description: MDR efflux pump, AedC ( Hassan et al. 2011 ). Shown to export chloramphenicol and tetracycline.

2.A.1.3.66.description: MFS permease of 413 aas and 12 TMSs. Encoded within the SoxR regulon; possibly a drug exporter ( Naseer et al. 2014 ).

2.A.1.3.72.description: Riboflavin transporter of 456 aas and 14 TMSs, RibZ ( Gutiérrez-Preciado et al. 2015 ).

2.A.1.3.82.description: Multidrug resistance transporter protein of 519 aas and 14 TMSs. It exports 2-thiocyanatopyridine derivatives ( Nunvar et al. 2019 ).

2.A.17.1.9.name: Di-/tripeptide transporter DtpT of 501 aas with 13 TMSs.
2.A.17.1.9.description: Di-/tripeptide transporter DtpT of 501 aas with 13 TMSs. DtpT plays an important role in biofilm formation and stress resistance in foodborne Staphylococcus aureus RMSA49 ( Wu et al. 2025 ).

2.A.17.4.7.name: Di-/Tri-peptide porter.
2.A.17.4.7.description: Di-/Tri-peptide porter. 3-d structure (PDB: 2XUT) known revealing a probable alternating access mechanism of transport ( Newstead et al. , 2011 ). A second structure shows the protein in an inward open conformation with the peptidommetic, alafosfalin, bound ( Guettou et al. 2013 ). Appears to take up glutathione ( Deutschbauer et al. 2011 ).

2.A.19.1.1.name: Ca 2+ :H + antiporter (also catalyzes Na + :H + and K + :H + antiport in processes that have been shown to be physiologically important under certain…
2.A.19.1.1.description: Ca 2+ :H + antiporter (also catalyzes Na + :H + and K + :H + antiport in processes that have been shown to be physiologically important under certain conditions) ( Ivey et al ., 1993 ; Radchenko et al ., 2006 )

2.A.19.2.2.name: Vacuolar [Mn 2+ or Ca 2+ ]:H + antiporter, Hum1 (Mn 2+ resistance (Mnr1)) protein.
2.A.19.2.2.description: Vacuolar [Mn 2+ or Ca 2+ ]:H + antiporter, Hum1 (Mn 2+ resistance (Mnr1)) protein. Vcx1 has 11 probable TMSs with the N-terminus inside ( Segarra and Thomas, 2008 ). The 3-d structure has been determined at 2.3 Å resolution for the cytosolic facing, substrate bound form, favoring the alternating access mechanism of transport ( Waight et al. 2013 ).

2.A.19.5.1.name: Putative Ca 2+ :H + or Ca 2+ :Na + antiporter with two 5 TMS internal repeats.
2.A.19.5.1.description: Putative Ca 2+ :H + or Ca 2+ :Na + antiporter with two 5 TMS internal repeats ( Sääf et al. 2001 ).

2.A.19.5.2.name: Cation (Ca 2+ /Na + ):proton antiporter, ChaA or CaxA (confers both Na + and Ca 2+ resistance)
2.A.19.5.2.description: Cation (Ca 2+ /Na + ):proton antiporter, ChaA or CaxA (confers both Na + and Ca 2+ resistance) ( Wei et al ., 2007 )

2.A.2.3.16.name: MfsD2B or SLC59A2 protein of 504 aas and 12 TMSs ().
2.A.2.3.16.description: MfsD2B or SLC59A2 protein of 504 aas and 12 TMSs (). It is a cation-dependent lipid transporter that specifically mediates export of sphingosine-1-phosphate from red blood cells and platelets ( Vu et al. 2017 ). Sphingosine-1-phosphate is a signaling sphingolipid, and its export from red blood cells into in the plasma is required for red blood cell morphology. It does not transport…

2.A.2.3.3.name: Isoprimeverose (α-D xylopyranosyl-(1,6)-D-glucopyranose) permease [xylose is not a substrate]
2.A.2.3.3.description: Isoprimeverose (α-D xylopyranosyl-(1,6)-D-glucopyranose) permease [xylose is not a substrate] ( Heuberger et al ., 2001 )

2.A.2.3.4.name: Probable α-xyloside uptake permease, YicJ
2.A.2.3.4.description: Probable α-xyloside uptake permease, YicJ ( Laikova et al ., 2001 )

2.A.2.3.5.name: Probable β-xyloside uptake permease, YagG
2.A.2.3.5.description: Probable β-xyloside uptake permease, YagG ( Laikova et al ., 2001 )

2.A.2.3.6.name: The putative cellobiose porter, BglT
2.A.2.3.6.description: The putative cellobiose porter, BglT ( Rodionov et al. 2010 )

2.A.2.3.7.name: The putative arabinoside porter, AraT
2.A.2.3.7.description: The putative arabinoside porter, AraT ( Rodionov et al. , 2010 )

2.A.2.3.8.name: Major Facilitator Superfamily Domain containing 2A, MFSD2A or SLC59A1 (543aas, 12 TMSs).
2.A.2.3.8.description: Major Facilitator Superfamily Domain containing 2A, MFSD2A or SLC59A1 (543aas, 12 TMSs). It is the omega-3-fatty acid transporter that plays a role in thermogenesis via β-adrenergic signaling. It takes up Tunicamycin (TM), a mixture of related species of nucleotide sugar analogs fatty-acylated with alkyl chains of varying lengths and degrees of unsaturation, produced by several Streptomyces…

2.A.2.5.2.name: The putative rhamnogalacturonide porter, RhiT.
2.A.2.5.2.description: The putative rhamnogalacturonide porter, RhiT ( Rodionov et al. 2004 ).

2.A.2.6.2.name: The maltose/maltooligosaccharide transporter, MalI (541 aas).
2.A.2.6.2.description: The maltose/maltooligosaccharide transporter, MalI (541 aas) ( Lohmiller et al ., 2008 ).

2.A.2.6.3.name: The putative maltose porter, MalT
2.A.2.6.3.description: The putative maltose porter, MalT ( Rodionov et al. , 2010 )

2.A.20.1.1.name: Low affinity P i or phosphate-zinc complex uptake transporter #1, PitA (K m =2 μM) (Me·P i :H + symporter).
2.A.20.1.1.description: Low affinity P i or phosphate-zinc complex uptake transporter #1, PitA (K m =2 μM) (Me·P i :H + symporter) ( Beard et al. 2000 ; Jackson et al. 2008 ). Also transports tellurite (TeO 3 2- ) slowly (Elías et al. 2012 ; Borghese et al. 2016 ).

2.A.20.1.2.name: Low affinity P i transporter #2, PitB (K m =30 μM) PitB, like PitA is also a Me·P i :H + symporter
2.A.20.1.2.description: Low affinity P i transporter #2, PitB (K m =30 μM) PitB, like PitA is also a Me·P i :H + symporter ( Borghese et al. 2016 )

2.A.20.1.5.name: Putative low affinity P i transporter PitH1, Sco4138.
2.A.20.1.5.description: Putative low affinity P i transporter PitH1, Sco4138 ( Santos-Beneit et al. 2008 ).

2.A.20.2.13.name: Putative sodium/phosphate symporter of 534 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.20.2.13.description: Putative sodium/phosphate symporter of 534 aas and 12 TMSs.

2.A.20.2.8.name: Na + :Pi transporter, SPT1
2.A.20.2.8.description: Na + :Pi transporter, SPT1 ( Li et al. , 2011 )

2.A.21.1.1.name: Pantothenate:Na + symporter, PanF.
2.A.21.1.1.description: Pantothenate:Na + symporter, PanF ( Vallari and Rock 1985 ; Jackowski and Alix 1990 ; Reizer et al. 1991 ).

2.A.21.2.1.name: Proline:Na + symporter, PutP.
2.A.21.2.1.description: Proline:Na + symporter, PutP ( Jung et al. , 2012 ). Extracellular loop 4 (eL4) controls periplasmic entry of substrate to the binding site ( Raba et al. 2014 ). Interactions between the tip of eL4 and the peptide backbone at the end of TMS 10 participate in coordinating conformational alterations underlying the alternating access mechanism of transport ( Bracher et al. 2016 ). TMS 6 plays a…

2.A.21.2.3.name: L-proline uptake porter, PutP.
2.A.21.2.3.description: L-proline uptake porter, PutP. Proline is used via this system as a carbon and nitrogen source. Induced by proline ( Johnson et al. 2008 ).

2.A.21.2.4.name: The high affinity nutritional proline uptake porter, PutP.
2.A.21.2.4.description: The high affinity nutritional proline uptake porter, PutP. PutP is inducible by external (but not internal) proline in a poorly defined process dependent on PutR ( Moses et al. 2012 ).

2.A.21.2.5.name: Proline uptake porter, OpuE (YerK).
2.A.21.2.5.description: Proline uptake porter, OpuE (YerK) ( von Blohn et al. 1997 ). Regulated by osmotic stress (high osmolarity). Induction involves σ B and σ A ( Spiegelhalter and Bremer 1998 ).

2.A.21.3.10.name: Na + -dependent, smf-driven, sialic acid transporter, STM1128 (NanP).
2.A.21.3.10.description: Na + -dependent, smf-driven, sialic acid transporter, STM1128 (NanP) ( Severi et al. , 2010 ). Also transports the related sialic acids, N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc) and 3-keto-3-deoxy-d-glycero-d-galactonononic acid (KDN) ( Hopkins et al. 2013 ).

2.A.21.3.2.name: Glucose or galactose:Na + symporter, SglS or SglT of 543 aas and 14 TMSs.
2.A.21.3.2.description: Glucose or galactose:Na + symporter, SglS or SglT of 543 aas and 14 TMSs ( Turk et al. 2006 ). The 3.0 Å structure is known ( Faham et al. , 2008 ). Sodium exit causes a reorientation of transmembrane helix 1 that opens an inner gate required for substrate exit ( Veenstra et al. 2004 ; Watanabe et al. , 2010 ). The involvement of aromatic residue pi interactions, especially with Na + binding, has…

2.A.21.3.20.name: NanT sialic acid transporter of 500 aas.
2.A.21.3.20.description: NanT sialic acid transporter of 500 aas ( Anba-Mondoloni et al. 2013 ).

2.A.21.3.21.name: Putative sugar:sodium symporter of 571 aas and 15 TMSs, YidK
2.A.21.3.21.description: Putative sugar:sodium symporter of 571 aas and 15 TMSs, YidK

2.A.21.3.7.name: Putative sialic acid uptake permease, NanP (D.A. Rodionov, pers. commun.)
2.A.21.3.7.description: Putative sialic acid uptake permease, NanP (D.A. Rodionov, pers. commun.)

2.A.21.3.8.name: The putative mannose porter, ManP ll.
2.A.21.3.8.description: The putative mannose porter, ManP ll ( Rodionov et al. 2010 ).

2.A.21.3.9.name: The putative galactose porter, GalP ll.
2.A.21.3.9.description: The putative galactose porter, GalP ll ( Rodionov et al. , 2010 ).

2.A.21.7.2.name: Acetate/glyoxylate/pyruvate permease, ActP or YjcG.
2.A.21.7.2.description: Acetate/glyoxylate/pyruvate permease, ActP or YjcG ( Gimenez et al ., 2003 ). Also transports tellurite (TeO 3 2- ) ( Elías et al. 2015 ). It may depend on the 2 TMS auxiliary subunit, YjcH (TC#9.B.136.1.1), the gene for which is adjacent to the yjcG gene ( Zhuge et al. 2019 ). Expression of these two genes is coordinately regulated and plays a role in the bacterial growth in macrophage…

2.A.21.7.4.name: Acetate uptake permease, ActP1; also takes up tellurite.
2.A.21.7.4.description: Acetate uptake permease, ActP1; also takes up tellurite ( Borghese and Zannoni 2010; Borghese et al. 2011 Borghese et al. 2011 ).

2.A.21.7.5.name: Acetate permease ActP-2/ActP2/ActP3.
2.A.21.7.5.description: Acetate permease ActP-2/ActP2/ActP3 ( Borghese and Zannoni 2010 ; Borghese et al. 2011 ). Also takes up tellurite (TeO 3 2- ) ( Borghese et al. 2016 ).

2.A.21.9.1.name: The nitrogen sensor-receptor domain of the CbrA sensor kinase
2.A.21.9.1.description: The nitrogen sensor-receptor domain of the CbrA sensor kinase

2.A.21.9.2.name: The proline sensor-receptor domain of the PrlS sensor kinase
2.A.21.9.2.description: The proline sensor-receptor domain of the PrlS sensor kinase

2.A.22.5.3.name: Neurotransmitter:sodium symporter of 455 aas, MhsT.
2.A.22.5.3.description: Neurotransmitter:sodium symporter of 455 aas, MhsT. The x-ray structures of two occluded inward-facing states with bound Na + ions and L-tryptophan have been solved (4US4; Malinauskaite et al. 2014). These structures provide insight into the cytoplasmic release of Na + . The switch from outward- to inward-oriented states is centered on the partial unwinding of transmembrane helix 5, facilitated…

2.A.22.5.5.name: Na + -dependent hypotaurine transporter of 454 aas and 11 TMSs.
2.A.22.5.5.description: Na + -dependent hypotaurine transporter of 454 aas and 11 TMSs ( Deutschbauer et al. 2011 ).

2.A.23.1.1.name: Glutamate/aspartate:H + symporter, GltP or GltT; has 8 TMSs with 2 re-entrant loops as for GltPh (TC# 2.A.23.1.5).
2.A.23.1.1.description: Glutamate/aspartate:H + symporter, GltP or GltT; has 8 TMSs with 2 re-entrant loops as for GltPh (TC# 2.A.23.1.5). GltP residues involved in substrate binding and transport have been identified, especially in transmembrane helices VII and VIII ( Rahman et al. 2016 ).

2.A.23.1.10.name: Organic acid uptake porter, DctA of 444 aas and 8 - 10 putative TMSs.
2.A.23.1.10.description: Organic acid uptake porter, DctA of 444 aas and 8 - 10 putative TMSs. Based on mutant analyses, it may transport succinate, benzoate, acetate, fumarate and malate ( Nam et al. 2003 ). A dctA mutant colonized tobacco roots to a lesser extent than the wild-type during early seedling development. Colonization by the dctA mutant, as compared to the wild type, also reduced the level of systemically…

2.A.23.1.14.name: Sodium:glutamate cotransporter (symporter), Glt, of 430 aas and probably 9 TMSs in a 3 + 3 + 3 TMS arrangement.
2.A.23.1.14.description: Sodium:glutamate cotransporter (symporter), Glt, of 430 aas and probably 9 TMSs in a 3 + 3 + 3 TMS arrangement. Several 3-d structures are known ( Jensen et al. 2013 ). The binding and transport of L- and D-aspartate have been studied, revealing that both the L- and D-aspartate bound Glt Tk structures with only minor rearrangements in the structure of the binding site ( Arkhipova et al. 2019 ). A…

2.A.23.1.15.name: Glutamate:Na + symporter, Glt, of 425 aas and 10 TMSs.
2.A.23.1.15.description: Glutamate:Na + symporter, Glt, of 425 aas and 10 TMSs. Pyrococcus horikoshii amino acid transporter Glt Ph revealed, like other channels and transporters, activity mode switching, previously termed wanderlust kinetics ( Jiang et al. 2024 ). Structural states were attributed to a functional timeline, allowing six structures to be solved from a single molecule, and an inward-facing state, IFS…

2.A.23.1.2.name: Glutamate/aspartate:Na + + H + symporter of 421 aas and 10 - 12 TMSs.
2.A.23.1.2.description: Glutamate/aspartate:Na + + H + symporter of 421 aas and 10 - 12 TMSs. By inferring ancestral prokaryotic transporter sequences during a change in the ion-coupling mechanism, Reddy et al. 2025 found an evolutionary transition from sodium-dependent to independent substrate binding and transport. Structural and functional experiments on ancestral transporters suggested that the transition involved…

2.A.23.1.3.name: C 4 -dicarboxylate transporter (substrates: fumarate, D- and L-malate, succinate, succinamide, orotate, iticonate, mesaconate).
2.A.23.1.3.description: C 4 -dicarboxylate transporter (substrates: fumarate, D- and L-malate, succinate, succinamide, orotate, iticonate, mesaconate). This protein is 85% identical to the Sinorhizobium melitoti ortholog, mutants of which have an alterred substrate specificity and inability to support N 2 fixing symbiosis ( Yurgel and Kahn 2005 ).

2.A.23.1.5.name: Archaeal aspartate transporter, Glt ph (GltPh) (3-D structure known; 3V8F and 3V8G).
2.A.23.1.5.description: Archaeal aspartate transporter, Glt ph (GltPh) (3-D structure known; 3V8F and 3V8G) ( Boudker et al ., 2007 ; Yernool et al ., 2004 ). Cotransports aspartate with 2 Na + ( Ryan et al. , 2009 ) or 3 Na+ ( Groeneveld and Slotboom, 2010 ) or 1Na + plus 1 H + plus 1 K + ( Machtens et al. 2015 ). Reyes et al. (2009) have solved the structure of the inward facing state by cysteine crosslinking. The…

2.A.23.1.6.name: The dicarboxylate (succinate, fumarate, malate and oxaloacetate):H + symporter, DctA (probably 3H + are transported per succinate taken up.
2.A.23.1.6.description: The dicarboxylate (succinate, fumarate, malate and oxaloacetate):H + symporter, DctA (probably 3H + are transported per succinate taken up ( Groeneveld et al. , 2010 ).

2.A.23.1.7.name: Aerobic dicarboxylate transporter, DctA.
2.A.23.1.7.description: Aerobic dicarboxylate transporter, DctA. Interacts with the DcuS sensor kinase ( Witan et al. , 2012 ). The interaction of DctA with DcuS has been studied extensively and reviewed ( Unden et al. 2016 ).

2.A.23.1.8.name: Cystine transporter, YdjN, of 463 aas.
2.A.23.1.8.description: Cystine transporter, YdjN, of 463 aas. Also transports L-selenaproline (L-selenazolidine-4-carboxylic acid) and L-selenocystine, both toxic analogues that inhibit growth of urinary tract pathogenic E. coli ( Deutch et al. 2014 ).

2.A.25.name: The Alanine or Glycine:Cation Symporter (AGCS) Family

2.A.25.1.10.name: Putative Ala/Gly transporter of 476 aas and 11 TMSs, YaaJ
2.A.25.1.10.description: Putative Ala/Gly transporter of 476 aas and 11 TMSs, YaaJ

2.A.25.1.3.name: Alanine:Na + symporter, AgcS
2.A.25.1.3.description: Alanine:Na + symporter, AgcS ( Moore and Leigh, 2005 )

2.A.25.1.4.name: The putative glycine porter, GlyP.
2.A.25.1.4.description: The putative glycine porter, GlyP. Regulated by Glycine riboswitch ( Rodionov et al. 2011 )

2.A.25.1.5.name: Amino-acid carrier protein, AlsT.
2.A.25.1.5.description: Amino-acid carrier protein, AlsT. Negatively regulated by TnrA ( Yoshida et al. 2003).

2.A.25.1.9.name: Probable Glycine/alanine/asparagine/glutamine uptake porter, AgcS.
2.A.25.1.9.description: Probable Glycine/alanine/asparagine/glutamine uptake porter, AgcS ( Bualuang et al. 2014 ).

2.A.26.name: The Branched Chain Amino Acid:Cation Symporter (LIVCS) Family

2.A.26.1.1.name: Branched chain amino acid: Na + symporter
2.A.26.1.1.description: Branched chain amino acid: Na + symporter

2.A.26.1.10.name: Branched chain amino acid transporter 2 of 439 aas and 12 TMSs, BrnQ.
2.A.26.1.10.description: Branched chain amino acid transporter 2 of 439 aas and 12 TMSs, BrnQ ( Guardiola et al. 1974 ). The brnQ gene can be mutated to give rise to threonine tolerance ( Radi et al. 2022 ). However the wild type protein takes up threonine (in addition to leucine, isoleucine and valine) but with low affinity and high flux ( Khozov et al. 2023 ).

2.A.27.1.1.name: Glutamate:Na + symporter, GltS, of 401 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.27.1.1.description: Glutamate:Na + symporter, GltS, of 401 aas and 12 TMSs. It transports L- and D-glutamate, α-methylglutamate and homocysteate. Swapping the order of the two halves (repeat units) does not decrease activity ( Dobrowolski and Lolkema, 2010 ).

2.A.27.1.5.name: sodium:glutamate symporter of 476 aas and 12 TMSs, GltS.
2.A.27.1.5.description: sodium:glutamate symporter of 476 aas and 12 TMSs, GltS. It has a K m for glutamate of 5 μM, but has low affinity for Na + . Glutamate uptake is inhibited by glu, gln, asp and asn ( Boonburapong et al. 2012 ).

2.A.27.2.1.name: Glutamate:sodium symporter, GltS.
2.A.27.2.1.description: Glutamate:sodium symporter, GltS ( Boonburapong et al. 2012 ).

2.A.28.2.4.name: Na + :bile acid symporter (AstB).
2.A.28.2.4.description: Na + :bile acid symporter (AstB). The 3-d structure is available (3ZUX).

2.A.28.2.6.name: Probable macrolide resistance porter (very similar to the orthologue in B. brevis ).
2.A.28.2.6.description: Probable macrolide resistance porter (very similar to the orthologue in B. brevis ) ( Margolles et al. 2005 ).

2.A.28.2.9.name: Sodium bile acid symporter family protein, ASBT, of 307 aas and 10 TMSs.
2.A.28.2.9.description: Sodium bile acid symporter family protein, ASBT, of 307 aas and 10 TMSs. The 3-d structure has been solved (4N7W and 4N7X) ( Zhou et al. 2014 ). This structure has been used to model the yeast Acr3 protein (TC# 2.A.59.1.1) which is in a distinct family of the BART superfamily ( Wawrzycka et al. 2016 ).

2.A.28.3.4.name: Putative Na + -dependent transporter, YfeH (332 aas; 7-10 TMSs)
2.A.28.3.4.description: Putative Na + -dependent transporter, YfeH (332 aas; 7-10 TMSs)

2.A.3.1.1.name: Phenylalanine:H + symporter, PheP of 458 aas and 12 established TMSs.
2.A.3.1.1.description: Phenylalanine:H + symporter, PheP of 458 aas and 12 established TMSs ( Pi and Pittard 1996 ; Pi et al. 2002 ). Catalytic residues have been identified ( Pi et al. 1993 ), and interhelical interactions have been proposed ( Dogovski et al. 2003 ).

2.A.3.1.13.name: Putrescine importer, PuuP
2.A.3.1.13.description: Putrescine importer, PuuP ( Kurihara et al ., 2005 )

2.A.3.1.19.name: Transporter of lysine, histidine and arginine, HisP or LysQ, of 477 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.19.description: Transporter of lysine, histidine and arginine, HisP or LysQ, of 477 aas and 12 TMSs ( Trip et al. 2013 ).

2.A.3.1.3.name: Aromatic amino acid:H + symporter, AroP of 457 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.1.3.description: Aromatic amino acid:H + symporter, AroP of 457 aas and 12 TMSs ( Cosgriff and Pittard 1997 ). Transports phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan ( Honoré and Cole 1990 ).

2.A.3.1.4.name: γ-aminobutyrate:H + symporter, GabP.
2.A.3.1.4.description: γ-aminobutyrate:H + symporter, GabP. It also transports a variety of pyridine carboxylates. Phosphatidylethanolamine is required for its proper topological organization( Zhang et al. 2005 ). GabP in citrus may also play a role in GABA uptake ( Nehela and Killiny 2025 ).

2.A.3.1.5.name: β-alanine/γ-aminobutyrate/proline/3,4-dehydroproline:H + symporter, GabP.
2.A.3.1.5.description: β-alanine/γ-aminobutyrate/proline/3,4-dehydroproline:H + symporter, GabP ( Ferson et al. 1996 ; Zaprasis et al. 2014 ). Also transports 3-aminobutyrate, 3-aminopropanoate, cis-4-aminobutenoate ( Brechtel and King 1998 ).

2.A.3.1.7.name: D-Serine/D-alanine/glycine/D-cycloserine:H + symporter.
2.A.3.1.7.description: D-Serine/D-alanine/glycine/D-cycloserine:H + symporter (regulated by the small RNA, GcvB; Pulvermacher et al. , 2009 ). The system is active after growth in minimal medium but not after growth in complex medium ( Baisa et al. 2013 ).

2.A.3.11.1.name: The aspartate uptake permease, YveA
2.A.3.11.1.description: The aspartate uptake permease, YveA (also transports L-aspartate hydroxamate and glutamate, and possibly asparagine and glutamine; Lorca et al ., 2003 )

2.A.3.13.3.name: L-Leucine uptake porter, YjeH, of 426 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.13.3.description: L-Leucine uptake porter, YjeH, of 426 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs ( Deutschbauer et al. 2011 ).

2.A.3.14.1.name: APC family member; Ala/Val/Leu-rich protein encoded within an operon that also encodes a 23S rRNA methyl transferase, RumA.
2.A.3.14.1.description: APC family member; Ala/Val/Leu-rich protein encoded within an operon that also encodes a 23S rRNA methyl transferase, RumA. Two half sized TrkA proteins are encoded within an operon that is divergently transcribed. Possibly, they regulate transport.

2.A.3.14.3.name: APC protein with 610 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.3.14.3.description: APC protein with 610 aas and 12 TMSs. 77% identical to an orthologue in Weissella viridescens that serves as a receptor or uptake transporter for the two peptide bacteriocin, plantaricin JK (1.C.30.1.1) ( Oppegård et al. 2016 ; Ekblad et al. 2017) .

2.A.3.2.1.name: Putrescine:ornithine antiporter for putrescine export; putrescine:H + symporter for uptake.
2.A.3.2.1.description: Putrescine:ornithine antiporter for putrescine export; putrescine:H + symporter for uptake ( Igarashi and Kashiwagi 1996 ). Modeling tools have been used to gain information about the structures and functions of CadB and PotE in E. coli ( Tomitori et al. , 2012 ).

2.A.3.2.5.name: Homodimeric electrogenic arginine (Km=80μM):agmatine antiporter, AdiC, involved in extreme acid resistance.
2.A.3.2.5.description: Homodimeric electrogenic arginine (Km=80μM):agmatine antiporter, AdiC, involved in extreme acid resistance ( Fang et al ., 2007 ; Gong et al ., 2003 ; Iyer et al ., 2003 ). A projection structure at 6.5 Å resolution has been published ( Casagrande et al. , 2008 ), and the 3.2 Å resolution X-ray structure was determined by Fang et al. , 2009 and Gao et al. , 2009 . Protonation of glutamate 208…

2.A.3.2.6.description: Putative lysine uptake permease, YvsH ( Rodionov et al ., 2003 )

2.A.3.8.17.name: Putative fructoselysine transporter FrlA.
2.A.3.8.17.description: Putative fructoselysine transporter FrlA ( Wiame and Van Schaftingen 2004 ). Also transports psicoselysine.

2.A.3.8.5.name: Cystine/glutamate antiporter, xCT (requires the 4F2hc protein (TC #8.A.9.2.1)).
2.A.3.8.5.description: Cystine/glutamate antiporter, xCT (requires the 4F2hc protein (TC #8.A.9.2.1)). Functions in the generation of glutathione and plays a role in the oxidative stress response ( Wang et al. 2015 ). xCT is involved in the export of intracellular glutamate in exchange for extracellular cystine. Glutamate is the main neurotransmitter in the retina and plays a key metabolic role as a major anaplerotic…

2.A.30.1.6.name: Solute carrier family 12 (potassium/chloride transporters), member 9.
2.A.30.1.6.description: Solute carrier family 12 (potassium/chloride transporters), member 9. Biallelic loss-of-function variants of SLC12A9 cause lysosome dysfunction and a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder ( Accogli et al. 2024 ). Upregulation of SLC12A3 and SLC12A9 confers aggressiveness and unfavorable prognosis in uveal melanoma ( Yan et al. 2023 ).

2.A.33.1.1.description: NhaA Na + :2H + antiporter (structure determined and mechanism proposed ( Williams, 2000 ; Hunte et al ., 2005 ; Olkhova et al ., 2006 ; Screpanti et al ., 2006 ; Arkin et al ., 2007 )). The K300R mutant is also electrogenic ( Călinescu et al. 2017 ). TMS II lines the cation passage, and Asp65 is critical for pH activation of the antiporter ( Herz et al. , 2010 ). NhaA is subject to pH-activation…

2.A.33.1.2.description: NhaA Na + ,K + :H + antiporter ( Radchenko et al ., 2006 )

2.A.34.1.1.description: NhaB Na + :H + antiporter of 513 aas and 11 or 12 TMSs. NhaB is physiologically important when the level of NhaA activity is growth limiting, when nhaA is not sufficiently induced, and/or when NhaA is not activated ( Pinner et al. 1993 ). The stoichiometry of NhaB is 3H + /2Na + , different from that of NhaA ( Pinner et al. 1994 ). It is required for intracellular pH regulation under alkaline…

2.A.34.1.2.name: NhaB Na + ,K + :H + antiporter
2.A.34.1.2.description: NhaB Na + ,K + :H + antiporter ( Radchenko et al ., 2006 )

2.A.34.1.3.description: Na + /H + antiporter that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons, NhaB of 500 aas. Can also extrude lithium in exchange for protons. Km values for Li + and Na + of 2.0 mM and 1.3 mM, respectively. The antiport activity was inhibited by amiloride with a Ki value of 0.04 mM ( Kuroda et al. 2004 ).

2.A.35.1.2.name: Malate + H + : lactate + Na + antiporter, MleN or YqkI of 468 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement.
2.A.35.1.2.description: Malate + H + : lactate + Na + antiporter, MleN or YqkI of 468 aas and 12 TMSs in a 6 + 6 TMS arrangement ( Wei et al. 2000 ).

2.A.35.1.5.description: The putative methionine porter, MetT. Regulated by S-adenosylmethionine-dependent repressor MetJ ( Rodionov et al. 2011 ).

2.A.35.1.6.description: YheL; TyrT, putative tyrosine uptake cation symporter; NhaC, putative Na + /H + antiporter (Sodium/hydrogen antiporter) ( Rodionov et al. 2004 ).

2.A.35.1.9.description: Predicted methioine:cation symporter of 459 aas and 12 TMSs, MetT ( Rodionov et al. 2004 ). Also called NhaC.

2.A.35.2.1.description: Na + /H + antiporter of the NhaC family

2.A.35.2.2.description: Putative lysine transporter, LysW. Regulated by Lysine riboswitch ( Rodionov et al. 2003 )

2.A.36.2.3.description: solute carrier family 9, subfamily B, SLC9B. (NHA1, cation proton antiporter 1). The SLC9 gene family encodes Na + /H + exchangers (NHEs), a group of membrane transport proteins critically involved in the regulation of cytoplasmic and organellar pH, cell volume, as well as systemic acid-base and volume homeostasis ( Anderegg et al. 2022 ). NHEs of the SLC9A subfamily (NHE 1-9) are well-known for…

2.A.36.3.1.description: Putative antiporter of 549 aas (function unknown) ( Verkhovskaya et al. 2001 ).

2.A.36.6.10.name: Na + /H + antiporter of 403 aas and 11 predicted TMSs, NhaH.
2.A.36.6.10.description: Na + /H + antiporter of 403 aas and 11 predicted TMSs, NhaH. Exchanges Na + or Li + but not K + for H + ( Zou et al. 2008 ). Confers Na + and Li + tolerance.

2.A.36.6.11.name: Na + /H + antiporter, NhaP2 (YcgO; CvrA) of 578 aas and 13 TMSs.
2.A.36.6.11.description: Na + /H + antiporter, NhaP2 (YcgO; CvrA) of 578 aas and 13 TMSs. Involved in growth at low osmolarity, intracellular K + maintenance, and volume regulation ( Verkhovskaya et al. 2001 ). Hyposaline xonsiriona induces oxidative stress and disrupts gut microbiome stability in C. notata , thereby triggering complex physiological and molecular responses ( Kim et al. 2025 ).

2.A.36.6.3.name: K + :H + antiporter, KhaP2 (NhaP2).
2.A.36.6.3.description: K + :H + antiporter, KhaP2 (NhaP2). Participates in volume control under low osmorality conditions ( Radchenko et al ., 2006 ; Resch et al. , 2010 )

2.A.36.6.4.description: The K + (NH 4 + ):H + antiporter, NhaP (confers alkali resistance for alkaline pH homeostasis) ( Wei et al ., 2007 )

2.A.36.6.5.name: K + :H + antiporter NhaP2. (84% identical to 2.A.36.6.3).
2.A.36.6.5.description: K + :H + antiporter NhaP2 (catalyzes K + :H + and Na + :H + exchange; Resch et al. , 2010 ). (84% identical to 2.A.36.6.3). A cation binding pocket in the middle of the membrane and a pathway leading to it have been identified ( Mourin et al. 2018 ). There are 3 NhaP types in Vibrio cholerae (Vc-NhaP1, 2, and 3). They are critical for maintenance of K + homeostasis in the cytoplasm, and all 3 are…

2.A.36.6.6.name: Na + /H + antiporter 1 (MjNhaP1).
2.A.36.6.6.description: Na + /H + antiporter 1 (MjNhaP1). NhaP1 is a dimer with 13 TMSs per monomer as revealed by electron crystalography of 2-d crystals ( Goswami et al. 2011 ). This structure is contrasted with that of the distantly related bacterial NhaA; these two structures are quite different in detail, but similar within the 6 TMS repeat unit. Asp234/235 of helix VIII are involved in ligand-binding, and helix X…

2.A.36.6.7.name: NhaH Na + /Li + /H + antiporter.
2.A.36.6.7.description: NhaH Na + /Li + /H + antiporter ( Yang et al. 2006 ).

2.A.36.6.8.name: Na + /H + antiporter of 424 aas, NhaP, that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons.
2.A.36.6.8.description: Na + /H + antiporter of 424 aas, NhaP, that extrudes sodium in exchange for external protons. Has weak (if any) Li + /H + antiport activity ( Kuroda et al. 2004 ).

2.A.36.6.9.name: Na + /H + antiporter, NhaP, of 443 aas.
2.A.36.6.9.description: Na + /H + antiporter, NhaP, of 443 aas. Several 3-d structures are known ( Wöhlert et al. 2014 ). The ion is coordinated by three acidic side chains, a water molecule, a serine and a main-chain carbonyl in an unwound stretch of TMS 5 at the deepest point of a negatively charged cytoplasmic funnel. A second narrow polar channel may facilitate proton uptake from the cytoplasm. Transport activity is…

2.A.36.7.1.name: ApNhaP: a Na + :H + antiporter at pH 5-9; a Ca 2+ :H + antiporter at alkaline pH (not an Li:H + antiporter).
2.A.36.7.1.description: ApNhaP: a Na + :H + antiporter at pH 5-9; a Ca 2+ :H + antiporter at alkaline pH (not an Li:H + antiporter) ( Waditee et al. 2001 ). When the gene for ApNhaP is expressed in the fresh water cyanobacterium, Synechococcus sp. PCC 7942, it became salt tolerant and could live in salt water ( Waditee et al. 2002 ; ).

2.A.36.7.2.description: Low affinity (Km=8 mM) Na + (Li + ):H + antiporter, NhaS1

2.A.37.2.4.description: The high-affinity (Km(Na + )=0.7 mM) Na + (Li + ):H + thylakoid membrane antiporter, NhaS3 (essential for growth; promotes Na + resistance; expressed in the presence of high CO 2 concentrations; under circadian control ( Tsunekawa et al. 2009 ).

2.A.37.3.3.description: Putative Na + :H + antiporter of 438 aas and 13 TMSs.

2.A.37.4.2.name: Endosome and prevacuole K + :H + antiporter, CHX17 of 820 aas and 13 putative TMSs.
2.A.37.4.2.description: Endosome and prevacuole K + :H + antiporter, CHX17 of 820 aas and 13 putative TMSs. Mediates potassium ion and pH homeomeostasis, thereby influencing membrane trafficking ( Chanroj et al. 2011 ). May also catalyze Na + /H + antiport ( Sze and Chanroj 2018 ). CHX can promote the uptake of K + , increase the ratio of K + /Na + , and promote the growth of plants under K + deficiency and treatment…

2.A.37.4.8.name: Endoplasmic reticular K + /H + antiporter, CHX20.
2.A.37.4.8.description: Endoplasmic reticular K + /H + antiporter, CHX20. Maintains pH and K + homeostasis in guard cells. Plays a critical role in osmoregulation through the control of stomates opening. Regulates alkaline pH-sensitive growth and influences membrane trafficking ( Chanroj et al. 2011 ).

2.A.38.1.1.name: K + uptake transporter (K + :H + symporter), TrkHA.
2.A.38.1.1.description: K + uptake transporter (K + :H + symporter), TrkHA. The 3-d structure of TrkH is known ( Cao et al. 2011 ). Molecular dynamics simulations of TrkH have been reported ( Domene and Furini, 2012 ). TrkA, which forms a tertameric ring that needs to bind ATP to activate transport, interacts with the Enzyme IIA Ntr of the PTS (TC# 4.A) which inhibits transport ( Lee et al. 2007 ).

2.A.38.1.2.description: K + uptake transporter, TrkIA (Km=1 mM) ( Kraegeloh et al ., 2005 )

2.A.38.4.3.description: Low affinity (1 mM) K + uptake transporter, KtrAB. 2.A.38.4.5.description: The Na + -dependent K + uptake transporter, KtrABE, required for adaption to salinity stress and high osmolarity ( Zulkifli et al. , 2010 ). KtrB alone confers low K + uptake activity; KtrA+KtrE are required for Na + dependency and higher K + uptake rates.

2.A.38.4.6.description: K + uptake system, KtrABD. S. aureus devoid of the Ktr system became sensitive to hyperosmotic conditions, exhibited a hyperpolarized plasma membrane, and increased susceptibility to aminoglycoside antibiotics and cationic antimicrobials. In contrast to other organisms, the S. aureus Ktr system was shown to be important for low-K+ growth under alkaline conditions but played only a minor role in…

2.A.39.1.2.description: The putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transporter, CytX ( Rodionov et al. 2002 )

The closely related Zea mays NCS1 transports adenine, guanine, and cytosine and competitively binds, 5-fluorocytosine, hypoxanthine, xanthine, and uric acid. 2.A.39.3.14.name: NCS1 of 528 aas and 12 TMSs.
2.A.39.3.14.description: NCS1 of 528 aas and 12 TMSs. Transporter of adenine, guanine, uracil and allantoin ( Schein et al. 2013 ).

2.A.39.3.4.name: Allantoin permease, PucI, with 12 TMSs and both N- and C-termini on the inside.
2.A.39.3.4.description: Allantoin permease, PucI, with 12 TMSs and both N- and C-termini on the inside. PucI transports allantoin with a Km of 24 mμM, but recognizes some additional hydantoin compounds, including hydantoin itself, and to a lesser extent a range of nucleobases and nucleosides ( Ma et al. 2016 ).

2.A.39.3.8.description: Allantoin permease; encoded in an operon with allantoinase and other degradative enzymes ( Moraes and Reithmeier 2012 ).

2.A.39.5.1.description: The putative mannitol porter, MtlP ( Rodionov et al. 2010 ).

2.A.4.1.4.description: Zn 2+ (Km=105 μM), Cd 2+ (Km=90 μM):proton (Km=20 nM) antiport metal ion efflux permease, ZitB ( Chao and Fu, 2004a ); Zn 2+ (Km=1.4 μM; Anton et al ., 2004 ). It also takes up Ni 2+ and Cu 2+ ( Rahman et al. , 2008 ).

2.A.4.1.7.description: Dimeric Zn 2+ efflux carrier of 299 aas and 5 TMSs, CzcD ( Martin and Giedroc 2016 ).

2.A.4.3.13.description: Zn 2+ , Fe 2+ and Co 2+ exporter, AitP, of 321 aas and 6 TMSs. The N 2 -fixing bacteria, Sinorhizobium meliloti , is a suitable model to determine the roles of Co 2+ -transporting Co-eCDF in Fe 2+ homeostasis because it has a putative member of this subfamily, AitP, and two specific Fe 2+ -export systems. An insertional mutant of AitP showed Co 2+ sensitivity and accumulation, Fe accumulation and…

2.A.4.4.7.description: Lead (Pb 2+ ) efflux transporter of 211 aas, PbtF ( Hložková et al. 2013 ).

2.A.4.7.1.description: Zn 2+ /Cd 2+ /Hg 2+ /Fe 2+ :H + antiporter, YiiP or FieF ( Chao and Fu, 2004b ; Grass et al ., 2005 ; Wei et al ., 2004 ; Wei and Fu, 2006 ). X-ray analyses of this fragment to 2.2 A resolution with and 1.7 A without zinc ions have been solved. The former has at least two zinc ions bound per monomer ( Höfer et al. 2007 )…

2.A.4.7.5.description: Cd 2+ /Zn 2+ efflux pump, YiiP or FieF. A low resolution structure in the open configuration has been determined by cryoelectron microscopy ( Coudray et al. 2013 ).

2.A.4.7.9.description: Ferrous iron detoxifying protein, FieF, of 337 aas and 6 TMSs. Also probably exports Zn 2+ , Co 2+ , Cd 2+ and Ni 2+ ( Munkelt et al. 2004 ).

2.A.40.1.1.description: Uracil permease, UraA. The crystal structure of UraA with bound uracil at 2.8 Å resolution is available (PDB: 3QE7) ( Lu et al. , 2011 ). UraA has a novel structural fold, with 14 TMSs divided into two inverted repeats. A pair of antiparallel β-strands is located between TMS3 and TMS10 and has an important role in structural organization and substrate recognition. The structure is spatially…

2.A.40.1.2.name: High affinity uracil permease.
2.A.40.1.2.description: High affinity uracil permease ( Martinussen et al. 2001 ).

2.A.40.1.3.description: P yrimidine transporter of broad specificity , RutG of 442 aas and 14 TMSs; transports both uracil and thymine with high affinity as well as, xanthine with low efficiency ( Loh et al. , 2006 ; Kim et al. 2010 ; Botou et al. 2018 ).

2.A.40.3.3.name: Uric acid (urate) permease YgfU.
2.A.40.3.3.description: Uric acid (urate) permease YgfU. YgfU exhibits low affinity (0.5 mM) but high capacity for urate and very poor activity for xanthine. Essential residues were identified. Coversion of Thr-100 to ala resulted in efficient xanthine transport ( Papakostas and Frillingos 2012 ).

2.A.40.4.2.description: The putative xanthine permease, YicE ( Karatza and Frillingos, 2005 )

2.A.40.4.3.description: The YgfO (XanQ) purine (xanthine) transporter. Residues involved in substrate binding have been identified ( Georgopoulou et al. , 2010 ). TMS3 functions in substrate recognition ( Karena and Frillingos, 2011 ). Many more essential residues have more recently been identified ( Karena et al. 2015 ). An "ancestral" homolog (AncXanQ) has been constructed and proved to have broader specificity…

2.A.40.4.6.name: XanQ or PbuX, purine base uptake porter specific for xanthine and guanine.
2.A.40.4.6.description: XanQ or PbuX, purine base uptake porter specific for xanthine and guanine. It is of 463 aas and 13 or 14 TMSs in a 5 + 3 or 4 +1 + 4 TMS arrangement ( Tatsaki et al. 2021 ).

2.A.40.7.2.name: Hypoxanthine/guanosine uptake transporter, PbuG
2.A.40.7.2.description: Hypoxanthine/guanosine uptake transporter, PbuG ( Johansen et al ., 2003 )

2.A.40.7.4.description: Adenine permease, YicO. Also recognizes with low micromolar affinity N(6)-benzoyladenine, 2,6-diaminopurine, and purines ( Papakostas et al. 2013 ).

2.A.40.7.5.name: Purine base permease, GhxP or YjcD.
2.A.40.7.5.description: Purine base permease, GhxP or YjcD. Transports purines such as guanine, hypoxanthine, and xanthine. Also transports mutagenic purines such as 6-N-hydroxylaminopurine (HAP), 2-amino-HAP (AHAP), 6-mercaptopurine, 6-thioguanine, 1-methylguanine, 8-azaguanine, 6-thioguanine and 2-aminopurine ( Kozmin et al. 2013 ; Papakostas et al. 2013 ).

2.A.40.7.6.description: Adenine permease, PurP. Also recognize with low micromolar affinity N(6)-benzoyladenine, 2,6-diaminopurine, and purine ( Papakostas et al. 2013 ).

2.A.40.7.7.description: Guanine/hypoxanthine uptake porter of 455 aas, GhxQ, YgfQ or YgfR. Also takes up mutagens such as 1-methylguanine, 8-azaguanine, 6-thioguanine, and 6-mercaptopurine ( Papakostas et al. 2013 ) and catalyzes dis-C3 (membrane-permeable, cationic fluorescent dye, the carbocyanine diS-C3 efflux ( Jindal et al. 2019 ).

2.A.40.7.8.description: NCS2 family permease of 429 aas and 13 apparent TMSs in a 7 + 6 TMS arrangement.

2.A.6.1.10.description: Putative Cu 2+ exporter, Czc2ABC. (induced by Cu 2+ and other heavy metal ions; Moraleda-Muñoz et al. , 2010 )

2.A.6.1.13.name: CzrABC Cd 2+ , Zn 2+ resistance efflux pump.
2.A.6.1.13.description: CzrABC Cd 2+ , Zn 2+ resistance efflux pump ( Hassan et al. , 1999 ).

2.A.6.1.14.name: CznABC Cd 2+ , Zn 2+ , Ni 2+ resistance efflux pump.
2.A.6.1.14.description: CznABC Cd 2+ , Zn 2+ , Ni 2+ resistance efflux pump. Required for urea modulation and gastric colonization ( Stähler et al. , 2006 ). CznC is an outer membrane porin ( Sedarat and Taylor-Robinson 2024 ).

2.A.6.1.15.name: The CzrCBA operon is induced by Cd 2+ and Zn 2+.
2.A.6.1.15.description: The CzrCBA operon is induced by Cd 2+ and Zn 2+ . CzrCBA transports Cd 2+ , Zn 2+ , and Co 2+ but not Ni 2+ (Valencia et al., 2013, in press).

2.A.6.1.16.name: The nczCBA operon (also called the czc operon) is induced maximally by Ni 2+ and Co 2+ , moderately by Zn 2+ but not by Cd 2+.
2.A.6.1.16.description: The nczCBA operon (also called the czc operon) is induced maximally by Ni 2+ and Co 2+ , moderately by Zn 2+ but not by Cd 2+ . NczCBA transports Ni 2+ Co 2+ and probably Zn 2+ and Cd 2+ ( Valencia et al. 2013 ).

2.A.6.1.18.name: Ni 2 , Co 2 exporter, NimA.
2.A.6.1.18.description: Ni 2 , Co 2 exporter, NimA. Functions with an MFP and an OMF (Nies, 2013, in Microbial Efflux Pumps, EW Yu, Q Zhang and MH Brown, editors, Caister Acadmic Press, 2013).

2.A.6.1.19.name: Co 2+ /Zn 2+ /Cd 2+ resistance RND protein of 1060 aas and 12 TMSs, CzcA.
2.A.6.1.19.description: Co 2+ /Zn 2+ /Cd 2+ resistance RND protein of 1060 aas and 12 TMSs, CzcA. It seems to play a role in Pb 2+ export ( Sun et al. 2024 ).

2.A.6.1.2.name: Heavy metal (Co 2+ , Zn 2+ , Cd 2+ ) efflux pump, CzcAB.
2.A.6.1.2.description: Heavy metal (Co 2+ , Zn 2+ , Cd 2+ ) efflux pump, CzcAB. Functions with CzcC (P13509; 1.B.17.2.2).

2.A.6.1.3.name: Silver ion (Ag + )-specific efflux pump of the RND family.
2.A.6.1.3.description: Silver ion (Ag + )-specific efflux pump of the RND family. 2.A.6.1.4.description: Cu + /Ag + efflux pump, CusABCF (may pump ions from the periplasm to the external medium); CusF is a periplasmic Cu + /Ag + binding receptor essential for full resistance ( Franke et al ., 2003 ). 2.A.6.1.5.description: The Zn 2+ , Cd 2+ , Pb 2+ exporter, CzcCBA1 (induced by Zn 2+ , Cd 2+ , Pb 2+ , Ni 2+ , Co 2+ and Hg 2+ ( Leedjarv et al ., 2007 ))

2.A.6.1.7.name: Putative Zn 2+ exporter, Cus1ABC
2.A.6.1.7.description: Putative Zn 2+ exporter, Cus1ABC (induced by Zn 2+ ; Moraleda-Muñoz et al. , 2010 )

2.A.6.1.8.name: Putative Cu 2+ exporter, Cus2ABC
2.A.6.1.8.description: Putative Cu 2+ exporter, Cus2ABC (induced by Cu 2+ ; Moraleda-Muñoz et al. , 2010 )
