3.A.1.14.11.description: The molybdate/tungstate ABC transporter, MolABC. For MolC; HI1470(C)/MolB; HI1471(M), the 3D structure is known at 2.4 Å resolution; Pinkett et al ., 2007 ). MolA binds to MolBC with low affinity (50 - 100μM), forming a transient complex that is stabilitzed by ligand binding ( Vigonsky et al. 2013 ).

3.A.1.14.12.name: Desferrioxamine B uptake porter, DesABC
3.A.1.14.12.description: Desferrioxamine B uptake porter, DesABC ( Barona-Gomez et al ., 2006 )

3.A.1.14.14.name: The Fe 3+ /Fe3 + ferrichrome/Fe 3+ heme uptake porter; SiuABDG (FtsABCD).
3.A.1.14.14.description: The Fe 3+ /Fe3 + ferrichrome/Fe 3+ heme uptake porter; SiuABDG (FtsABCD) ( Montañez et al. , 2005 ; Hanks et al. 2005 ; Li et al. 2013 ). A similar system has been characterized in S. iniae ( Wang et al. 2013 ).

3.A.1.14.16.name: The heme-specific uptake porter, HemTUV.
3.A.1.14.16.description: The heme-specific uptake porter, HemTUV ( Létoffé et al. , 2008 ).

3.A.1.14.18.name: The heme uptake porter, ShuTUV.
3.A.1.14.18.description: The heme uptake porter, ShuTUV ( Burkhard and Wilks, 2008 ). Transports a single heme per reaction cycle ( Mattle et al. , 2010 ). (3-d structure of ShuT is known (2RG7).

3.A.1.14.19.name: Heme uptake porter, HugBCD; also called HmuTUV.
3.A.1.14.19.description: Heme uptake porter, HugBCD ( Villarreal et al. , 2008 ); also called HmuTUV.

3.A.1.14.20.name: Heme-iron (hemin) utilization transporter BhuTUV.
3.A.1.14.20.description: Heme-iron (hemin) utilization transporter BhuTUV ( Brickman et al. , 2006 ; Vanderpool and Armstrong, 2004 ). The crystal structures of BhuUV with or without the periplasmic haem-binding protein BhuT have been solved ( Naoe et al. 2016 ). The TMSs show an inward-facing conformation, in which the cytoplasmic gate of the haem translocation pathway is completely open. Since this conformation is…

3.A.1.14.21.name: The heme uptake porter, PhuTUV (transports one heme per reaction cycle).
3.A.1.14.21.description: The heme uptake porter, PhuTUV (transports one heme per reaction cycle) ( Mattle et al. , 2010 ).

3.A.1.14.22.name: The putative ferric iron-desferrioxamine E uptake porter, DesEFGH.
3.A.1.14.22.description: The putative ferric iron-desferrioxamine E uptake porter, DesEFGH. The DesE binding receptor has been characterized ( Barona-Gómez et al. 2006 ). The remaining three ( desFGH ) genes cluster together without a gene encoding a receptor (R). They are believed to function with DesE based on sequence similarity and phylogenetic analyses (Getsin et al., 2013).

3.A.1.14.23.name: Two components of a vitamin B12 (cobalamin) uptake porter, BtuCD.
3.A.1.14.23.description: Two components of a vitamin B12 (cobalamin) uptake porter, BtuCD. BtuAB must exist but have not been identified ( Deutschbauer et al. 2011 ).

3.A.1.14.24.name: FecB1CDE iron siderophore uptake transporter.
3.A.1.14.24.description: FecB1CDE iron siderophore uptake transporter. Transports iron chelated dihydroxamate xenosiderophores, either ferric schizokinen (FeSK) or a ferric siderophore of the filamentous cyanobacterium Anabaena variabilis ATCC 29413 (a schizokinen derivative, SAV), as the sole source of iron in a TonB-dependent manner ( Obando S et al. 2018 ). The gene schT encodes the TonB-dependent outer membrane…

3.A.1.14.25.name: Heme uptake porter with three subunits.
3.A.1.14.25.description: Heme uptake porter with three subunits ( Mandal et al. 2019 ).

3.A.1.14.26.name: Cyanocobalamin uptake porter with 3 components, R, M and C.
3.A.1.14.26.description: Cyanocobalamin uptake porter with 3 components, R, M and C ( Mandal et al. 2019 ).

3.A.1.14.27.name: Heme transporter with three components, HmuU (M), HmuV (C) and HmuT (R).
3.A.1.14.27.description: Heme transporter with three components, HmuU (M), HmuV (C) and HmuT (R). Chemo-mechanical coupling in the transport cycle has been proposed with outward open, inward open and occluded states ( Tamura et al. 2019 ).

3.A.1.14.3.name: Iron (Fe 3+ )-hydroxamate (ferrichrome, coprogen, aerobactin, ferrioxamine B, schizakinen, rhodotorulic acid) porter, albomycin porter.
3.A.1.14.3.description: Iron (Fe 3+ )-hydroxamate (ferrichrome, coprogen, aerobactin, ferrioxamine B, schizakinen, rhodotorulic acid) porter, albomycin porter. A FtsZ inhibitor can utilize siderophore-ferric iron uptake transporter systems, FepA, CirA (outer membrane transporters) and FhuBC (inner membrane transporter) for activity against Gram-negative bacterial pathogens ( Bryan et al. 2024 ).

3.A.1.14.5.name: Heme (hemin) uptake porter.
3.A.1.14.5.description: Heme (hemin) uptake porter. The receptor, HmuT, binds two parallel stacked heme molecules, and two are transported per reaction cycle ( Mattle et al. , 2010 ).

3.A.1.14.7.name: Iron (Fe 3+ )-hydroxamate porter (transports Fe 3+ -ferrichrome and Fe 3+ -ferrioxamine B with FhuD1, and these compounds plus aerobactin and…
3.A.1.14.7.description: Iron (Fe 3+ )-hydroxamate porter (transports Fe 3+ -ferrichrome and Fe 3+ -ferrioxamine B with FhuD1, and these compounds plus aerobactin and coprogen with FhuD2). FhuB may function with FhuG (A6QEV8) together with FhuD2 to form a ferrichrome transporter where FhuB and FhuG have conserved arginine residues (R71 and R61, respectively) that form essential salt bridges with FhuD2 ( Vinés et al. 2013…

3.A.1.14.8.name: The iron-vibrioferrin uptake porter
3.A.1.14.8.description: The iron-vibrioferrin uptake porter ( Tanabe et al ., 2003 )

3.A.1.14.9.name: The Corrinoid porter, BtuCDE
3.A.1.14.9.description: The Corrinoid porter, BtuCDE ( Woodson et al ., 2005 )

3.A.1.140.1.name: The FtsX/FtsE ABC transporter (FtsX is of the type III topology).
3.A.1.140.1.description: The FtsX/FtsE ABC transporter ( Arends et al., 2009 ) (FtsX is of the type III topology). FtsEX directly recruits EnvC to the septum via an interaction between EnvC and a periplasmic loop of FtsX. FtsEX variants predicted to be ATPase defective still recruit EnvC to the septum but fail to promote cell separation. Amidase activation via EnvC in the periplasm is regulated by conformational changes…

3.A.1.140.2.name: The cell division ABC system, FtsX/FtsE
3.A.1.140.2.description: The cell division ABC system, FtsX/FtsE

3.A.1.140.4.name: Cell division ABC system, FtsXE of 300 aas and 4 TMSs, and 229 aas and 0 TMSs, respectively.
3.A.1.140.4.description: Cell division ABC system, FtsXE of 300 aas and 4 TMSs, and 229 aas and 0 TMSs, respectively.

3.A.1.140.6.name: Cell division system, FtsXE.
3.A.1.140.6.description: Cell division system, FtsXE. The FtsEX:PcsB complex forms a molecular machine that carries out peptidoglycan (PG) hydrolysis during normal cell division. FtsEX transduces signals from the cell division apparatus to stimulate PG hydrolysis by PcsB, an amidase, which interacts with extracellular domains of FtsX ( Bajaj et al. 2016 ).

3.A.1.140.8.name: FtsEX of Bacillus subtilis where FtsE is an ATPase of 228 aas (O34814) and FtsX is a dimeric membrane protein of 296 aas and 4 TMSs in a 1 + 3 TMS…
3.A.1.140.8.description: FtsEX of Bacillus subtilis where FtsE is an ATPase of 228 aas (O34814) and FtsX is a dimeric membrane protein of 296 aas and 4 TMSs in a 1 + 3 TMS arrangement (O34876). It is an ABC transporter secondarily involved in sporulation. It was initially thought to act as an importer and/or exporter, possibly at the top of a hierarchical cascade leading to the correct temporal initiation of sporulation…

3.A.1.141.name: The Ethyl Viologen Exporter (EVE) Family (DUF990 Family)

3.A.1.141.1.name: The ethyl (methyl; benzyl) viologen export pump, EvrABC (EvrB and EvrC of 6 TMSs are members of the large DUF990 superfamily; They appear to be of…
3.A.1.141.1.description: The ethyl (methyl; benzyl) viologen export pump, EvrABC (EvrB and EvrC of 6 TMSs are members of the large DUF990 superfamily ( Prosecka et al. , 2009 ); They appear to be of the ABC-2 topological type).

3.A.1.142.2.name: ABC exporter, YvfS/YvfR of 284 and 287 aas, respectively
3.A.1.142.2.description: ABC exporter, YvfS/YvfR of 284 and 287 aas, respectively

3.A.1.142.3.name: Uncharacterized ABC2 exporter consisting of a 6 TMS membrane protein of 254 aas and an ATPase, encoded by the gene adjacent to the 6 TMS membrane…
3.A.1.142.3.description: Uncharacterized ABC2 exporter consisting of a 6 TMS membrane protein of 254 aas and an ATPase, encoded by the gene adjacent to the 6 TMS membrane protein.

3.A.1.144.1.name: Functionally uncharacterized ABC2 transporter #1.
3.A.1.144.1.description: Functionally uncharacterized ABC2 transporter #1. This system is encoded by two genes that overlap and are therefore probably translationally coupled; they are in the same operon with the genes for 2.A.1.144.2.

3.A.1.144.2.name: Functionally uncharacterized ABC2 transporter #2.
3.A.1.144.2.description: Functionally uncharacterized ABC2 transporter #2. This system is encoded by two genes that overlap and are therefore probably translationally coupled; they are in the same operon with the genes for 2.A.1.144.1.

3.A.1.147.1.name: Putative two component ABC exporter with a membrane protein of 573 aas and 12 TMSs and an ATPase encoded adjacent to the membrane protein and also…
3.A.1.147.1.description: Putative two component ABC exporter with a membrane protein of 573 aas and 12 TMSs and an ATPase encoded adjacent to the membrane protein and also adjacent to a gene encoding an adenine glycosylase, probably within a single operon.

3.A.1.147.2.name: Putative 2-component sporulation-related ABC exporter.
3.A.1.147.2.description: Putative 2-component sporulation-related ABC exporter. The genes encoding this system are adjacent to a spore germination receptor (TC# 2.A.3.9.5) and a putative signalling molecule transporter (2.A.86.1.11) .

3.A.1.148.4.name: Uncharacterized ABC transporter, AbcYZ [Y (D2BBE4) = M with 6 TMSs; Z (D2BBE3)= C.]
3.A.1.148.4.description: Uncharacterized ABC transporter, AbcYZ [Y (D2BBE4) = M with 6 TMSs; Z (D2BBE3)= C.]

3.A.1.15.name: The Manganese/Zinc/Iron Chelate Uptake Transporter (MZT) Family (Similar to 3.A.1.12, 3.A.1.14 and 3.A.1.16)

3.A.1.15.11.name: The zinc uptake porter, YcdHI-YceA; AdcA/AdcC/AdcB.
3.A.1.15.11.description: The zinc uptake porter, YcdHI-YceA; AdcA/AdcC/AdcB ( Gaballa et al. , 2002 ).

3.A.1.15.12.name: Metal ion (probably iron) uptake permease , YtgABC-RD.
3.A.1.15.12.description: Metal ion (probably iron) uptake permease , YtgABC-RD. The third gene in the ytg operon is fused, the N-terminal membrane domain being fused to the C-terminal transcriptional regulator homologous to the diphtheria toxin repressor, DtxR. These two domains may be proteolitically processed yielding the two active proteins ( Thompson et al. 2012 ).

3.A.1.15.13.name: The ZnuA18/ZnuA08/ZnuB/ZnuC zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake system.
3.A.1.15.13.description: The ZnuA18/ZnuA08/ZnuB/ZnuC zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake system ( Hudek et al. 2013 ). ZnuB (M) and ZnuC (C) can function with either of two zinc ion receptors, ZnuA18 (R) which is encoded in the znuACB operon, and ZnuA08 (R) which is encoded elsewhere on the chromosome. ZnuA18 is more efficient that ZnuA08 in promoting uptake ( Hudek et al. 2013 ).

3.A.1.15.14.name: High affinity Mn 2+ uptake complex, PsaABC.
3.A.1.15.14.description: High affinity Mn 2+ uptake complex, PsaABC ( Lisher et al. 2013 ). The crystal structure of the manganese transporter PsaBC from Streptococcus pneumoniae has been solved in an open-inward conformation ( Neville et al. 2021 ). The type II transporter has a tightly closed transmembrane channel due to "extracellular gating" residues that prevent water permeation and ion reflux. Below these residues…

3.A.1.15.15.name: High affinity Mn 2+ uptake complex, MntABC.
3.A.1.15.15.description: High affinity Mn 2+ uptake complex, MntABC. The 3-d structure of MntC has been solved to 2.2Å resolution ( Gribenko et al. 2013 ).

3.A.1.15.18.name: ABC high affinity Zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake porter, ZnuABC.
3.A.1.15.18.description: ABC high affinity Zinc (Zn 2+ ) uptake porter, ZnuABC. The similar system from Y. pestis has been characterized ( Bobrov et al. 2014 ; Neupane et al. 2018 ). ZnuA (R) of that systems can bind up to 5 zinc ions with high affinity.

3.A.1.15.19.name: Zinc ion ABC uptake system, AztABCD, where AztD is a periplasmic chaparone protein that feeds Zn 2+ into AztC, the periplasmic receptor/binding…
3.A.1.15.19.description: Zinc ion ABC uptake system, AztABCD, where AztD is a periplasmic chaparone protein that feeds Zn 2+ into AztC, the periplasmic receptor/binding protein for the transporter ( Neupane et al. 2018 ).

3.A.1.15.20.name: ABC uptake transporter specific for Mn 2+ and Fe 2+ , SloABC.
3.A.1.15.20.description: ABC uptake transporter specific for Mn 2+ and Fe 2+ , SloABC ( Paik et al. 2003 ). The system is repressed by Mn 2+ together with the SloR repressor, encoded by a gene downstream of sloABC .

3.A.1.15.21.name: Mn 2+ ABC uptake system, MntABC.
3.A.1.15.21.description: Mn 2+ ABC uptake system, MntABC. Titratable transmembrane residues and a hydrophobic plug are essential for manganese import via the Bacillus anthracis ABC transporter MntBC-A ( Kuznetsova et al. 2021 ). Zinc is a high-affinity inhibitor. The transmembrane metal permeation pathway is lined with six titratable residues that can coordinate the positively charged metal, and mutagenesis studies…

3.A.1.15.4.name: Iron, Manganese (and Zinc) (Fe 2+ , Mn 2+ and Zn 2+ ) porter, YfeABCD.
3.A.1.15.4.description: Iron, Manganese (and Zinc) (Fe 2+ , Mn 2+ and Zn 2+ ) porter, YfeABCD. The periplasmic receptor, YfeA binds Zn(II) ions as a preferred substrate, even though the YfeABCD system most likely does not transport zinc ( Orzel et al. 2026 ). YfeA possesses two metal-binding sites. Site 2 was shown to bind Zn(II) and Mn(II), but not Fe(II) ions. Orzel et al. 2026 investigated the metal-binding…

3.A.1.15.5.name: Zinc (Zn 2+ ) porter of E. coli , ZnuABC.
3.A.1.15.5.description: Zinc (Zn 2+ ) porter of E. coli , ZnuABC. Required for Zn 2+ homeostasis and virulence in the close E. coli relative, Salmonella enterica (Ammendola et al ., 2007 ).

3.A.1.15.7.name: Manganese (Mn 2+ ) (Km=0.1 μM) and iron (Fe 2+ ) (5 μM) porter (inhibited by Cd 2+ > Co 2+ > Ni 2+ , Cu 2+ ) (most similar to YfeABCD of Yersinia…
3.A.1.15.7.description: Manganese (Mn 2+ ) (Km=0.1 μM) and iron (Fe 2+ ) (5 μM) porter (inhibited by Cd 2+ > Co 2+ > Ni 2+ , Cu 2+ ) (most similar to YfeABCD of Yersinia pestis (TC #3.A.1.15.4)). Important for virulence in Salmonella ( Karlinsey et al. , 2010 ).

3.A.1.15.8.name: Manganese (Mn 2+ ), zinc (Zn 2+ ) and possibly iron (Fe 2+ ) uptake porter, TroABCD.
3.A.1.15.8.description: Manganese (Mn 2+ ), zinc (Zn 2+ ) and possibly iron (Fe 2+ ) uptake porter, TroABCD ( Hazlett et al ., 2003 ). Transcription of the operon is controlled by the Mn 2+ -activated (not Zn 2+ - or Fe 2+ -activated) repressor, TroR (153 aas, acc# F7IW50;) TroR contains a metal-binding domain homologous to the YtgC-R protein (3.A.1.15.12) which has the membrane domain of this ABC transporter…

3.A.1.15.9.name: Manganese (Mn 2+ ) and Iron (Fe 2+ ) porter, SitABCD.
3.A.1.15.9.description: Manganese (Mn 2+ ) and Iron (Fe 2+ ) porter, SitABCD ( Davies and Walker, 2007 ). Both this system and the MntH system in Agrobacterium tumefaciens , both Mn 2+ transporters, are stronly inhibited by thymol and carvacrol, constituents of plant thyme white essential oils ( Jung et al. 2025 ). Other oil constituents are also inhibitory ( Jung et al. 2025 ).

3.A.1.152.1.name: LPS export system, LptF (M), LptG (M) and LptB (C).
3.A.1.152.1.description: LPS export system, LptF (M), LptG (M) and LptB (C). This system is also listed in TCDB under TC#1.B.42.1.2 as part of a multicomponent system. The entire system is described in detail there. LptB 2 FG extracts LPSs from the IM and transports them to the outer membrane. Luo et al. 2017 reported the crystal structure of nucleotide-free LptB2FG from P. aeruginosa . It shows that LPS transport…

3.A.1.152.10.name: Probable LptF/G or YjgP/Q membrane proteins of an ABC exporter, possibly specific for a lipopolysaccharide.
3.A.1.152.10.description: Probable LptF/G or YjgP/Q membrane proteins of an ABC exporter, possibly specific for a lipopolysaccharide. Adjacent genes code for proteases/peptidases. An ATPase that energizes this system has not been identified. The two membrane proteins are of 360 and 380 aas with 6 TMSs in a 3 + 3 TMS arrangement, separated by a large hydrophilic loop. Members of this family often work together with outer…

3.A.1.152.3.name: Uncharacterized ABC system of the YjgP/Q family; the two membrane proteins are encoded by adjacent genes, but the gene for the ATPase was not found.
3.A.1.152.3.description: Uncharacterized ABC system of the YjgP/Q family; the two membrane proteins are encoded by adjacent genes, but the gene for the ATPase was not found. However, a soluble OstA homologue (Q5SL97) of 824 aas is encoded adjacent to the two membrane protein-encoding genes.

3.A.1.152.4.name: Uncharacterized YjgP/YjgQ family homologue of 441 aas and 6 TMSs.
3.A.1.152.4.description: Uncharacterized YjgP/YjgQ family homologue of 441 aas and 6 TMSs. No other YjgP homologue and no ATPase is encoded adjacent to the gene encoding this protein.

3.A.1.152.5.name: Uncharacterized YjgP/Q homologue of 266 aas and 6 TMSs.
3.A.1.152.5.description: Uncharacterized YjgP/Q homologue of 266 aas and 6 TMSs. No ATPase or another YjgP homologue is encoded by a gene adjacent to this one.

3.A.1.152.7.name: YjgP/Q family protein of 392 aas and 6 TMSs
3.A.1.152.7.description: YjgP/Q family protein of 392 aas and 6 TMSs

3.A.1.152.9.name: Lipopolysaccharide transporter that exports LPS from the external surface of the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer membrane, LptB 2 FG.
3.A.1.152.9.description: Lipopolysaccharide transporter that exports LPS from the external surface of the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer membrane, LptB 2 FG. The 134-kDa protein complex is unique among ABC transporters because it extracts lipopolysaccharide from the external leaflet of the inner membrane and propels it along a filament that extends across the periplasm to directly deliver lipopolysaccharide into the…

3.A.1.156.3.name: ABC2 transporter of unknown substrate specificity with two membrane constituents and one ATPase.
3.A.1.156.3.description: ABC2 transporter of unknown substrate specificity with two membrane constituents and one ATPase.

3.A.1.158.2.name: Putative ABC-type multidrug transport system with 3 protein components.
3.A.1.158.2.description: Putative ABC-type multidrug transport system with 3 protein components.

3.A.1.159.2.name: Putative 12 TMS ABC permease of 534 aas, HalU.
3.A.1.159.2.description: Putative 12 TMS ABC permease of 534 aas, HalU ( Besse et al. 2015 ). The gene adjacent to the membrane protein gene is the putative ATPase gene.

3.A.1.16.name: The Nitrate/Nitrite/Cyanate Uptake Transporter (NitT) Family (Similar to 3.A.1.12 and 3.A.1.17)

3.A.1.16.1.name: Four component nitrate/nitrite porter.
3.A.1.16.1.description: Four component nitrate/nitrite porter ( Kikuchi et al. 1996 ). It's synthesis occurs in response to nitrite, not nitrate in a nitrate reductase mutant ( Kikuchi et al. 1996 ).

3.A.1.16.2.name: Bispecific cyanate/nitrite transporter.
3.A.1.16.2.description: Bispecific cyanate/nitrite transporter (functions in both cyanate and nitrite assimilation; Maeda and Omata, 2009 ).

3.A.1.16.3.name: Bicarbonate porter (activated by low [CO 2 ] mediated by CmpR;)
3.A.1.16.3.description: Bicarbonate porter (activated by low [CO 2 ] mediated by CmpR; ( Nishimura et al ., 2008 ))

3.A.1.16.4.name: Nitrate uptake system, NrtABCD.
3.A.1.16.4.description: Nitrate uptake system, NrtABCD ( Frías et al. , 1997 ). Molecular interactions within the nitrate uptake system of Anabaena PCC7120 have been reported (but are a bit confusing) ( Swapnil et al. 2021 ).

3.A.1.17.name: The Taurine Uptake Transporter (TauT) Family (Similar to 3.A.1.12 and 3.A.1.16)

3.A.1.17.10.name: Aliphatic sulfonate (alkanesulfonate) import permease, SsuABC (YcbOEM) and is regluated by the transcriptional activator, Cbl.
3.A.1.17.10.description: Aliphatic sulfonate (alkanesulfonate) import permease, SsuABC (YcbOEM) and is regluated by the transcriptional activator, Cbl ( van Der Ploeg et al. 1999 ; Eichhorn and Leisinger 2001 ).

3.A.1.17.11.name: Putative ABC transporter specific for riboflavin, RibXYZ.
3.A.1.17.11.description: Putative ABC transporter specific for riboflavin, RibXYZ. RibY is called " NMT1/THI5 like domain protein" ( Anderson et al. 2015 ).

3.A.1.17.12.name: Sulfonate and sulfonate ester uptake transporter, SsuABC.
3.A.1.17.12.description: Sulfonate and sulfonate ester uptake transporter, SsuABC ( Koch et al. 2005 ).

3.A.1.17.13.name: Putative thiamine (vitamin B 1 )-specific transporter, ThiXYZ.
3.A.1.17.13.description: Putative thiamine (vitamin B 1 )-specific transporter, ThiXYZ ( Rodionova et al. 2015 ).

3.A.1.17.3.name: Putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transport system, ThiXYZ.
3.A.1.17.3.description: Putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transport system, ThiXYZ ( Rodionov et al. , 2002 ). Regulated by TPP (thiamin) riboswitch. Potentially takes up a pyrimidine moiety of thiamin.

3.A.1.17.4.name: The taurine uptake system, TauABC.
3.A.1.17.4.description: The taurine uptake system, TauABC ( Krejcík et al. , 2008 ).

3.A.1.17.5.name: The phthalate uptake system, OphFGH.
3.A.1.17.5.description: The phthalate uptake system, OphFGH ( Chang et al. 2009 ).

3.A.1.17.6.name: Putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transport system, ThiXYZ.
3.A.1.17.6.description: Putative hydroxymethylpyrimidine transport system, ThiXYZ ( Rodionov et al. , 2002 ). Regulated by TPP (thiamin) riboswitch. Potentially takes up a pyrimidine moiety of thiamin. ThiY is homologous to the yeast THI5 HMP-P synthase (P43534) ( Bale et al. , 2010 ).

3.A.1.17.7.name: Putative riboflavin transport system, RibXY.
3.A.1.17.7.description: Putative riboflavin transport system, RibXY. Regulated by an FMN riboswitch ( Vitreschak et al. 2002 ).

3.A.1.17.8.name: Putative thiamine transport system, ThiXYZ.
3.A.1.17.8.description: Putative thiamine transport system, ThiXYZ ( Rodionov et al. , 2002 ). Regulated by TPP (thiamin) riboswitch.

3.A.1.17.9.name: Uncharacterized membrane protein of 733 aas and 12 TMSs.
3.A.1.17.9.description: Uncharacterized membrane protein of 733 aas and 12 TMSs. The other constituents of the system have not been identified.

3.A.1.18.1.name: Putative ECF transporter, EcfSTA; regulated by a cobalamin riboswitch.
3.A.1.18.1.description: Putative ECF transporter, EcfSTA; regulated by a cobalamin riboswitch.

3.A.1.19.name: The Thiamin Uptake Transporter (ThiT) Family (Most similar to 3.A.1.10, 3.A.1.6 and 3.A.1.8 in that order)

3.A.1.19.1.name: Thiamin, thiamin monophosphate and thiamin pyrophosphate porter.
3.A.1.19.1.description: Thiamin, thiamin monophosphate and thiamin pyrophosphate porter. The 2.25 Å structure of ThiB (TbpA) has been solved ( Soriano et al ., 2008 ).

3.A.1.19.2.name: The thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) uptake porter.
3.A.1.19.2.description: The thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) uptake porter ( Bian et al. , 2011 ).

3.A.1.19.3.name: ABC transporter of unknown function.
3.A.1.19.3.description: ABC transporter of unknown function. The three genes encoding this system are adjacent to a gene homologous to a mycothiol maleylpyruvate isomerase.

3.A.1.19.4.name: The putative sulfate/thiosulfate transporter, YnjBCD.
3.A.1.19.4.description: The putative sulfate/thiosulfate transporter, YnjBCD. YnjB has 12 TMSs. The three genes encoding this system are adjacent to one encoding a thiosulfate:sulfur transferase or a rhodanese (B7L6N1). Also considered to be a thiamine transporter ( Moussatova et al. 2008 ).

3.A.1.19.5.name: Putative ABC transporter, WtpB1/C1: molybdate/tungstate transport system.
3.A.1.19.5.description: Putative ABC transporter, WtpB1/C1: molybdate/tungstate transport system.

3.A.1.2.1.name: Ribose porter.
3.A.1.2.1.description: Ribose porter. RbsA has two ATPase domains fused together; RbsB is the substrate receptor; RbsC has 10 TMSs with N- and C-termini in the cytoplasm and forms a dimer ( Stewart and Hermodson, 2003 ). ABC importers can be divided into two classes. Type I importers follow an alternating access mechanism driven by the presence of the substrate. Type II importers accept substrates in a nucleotide-free…

3.A.1.2.10.name: The purine nucleoside permease (probably transports guanosine, adenosine, 2'-deoxyguanosine, inosine and xanthosine with decreasing affinity in this…
3.A.1.2.10.description: The purine nucleoside permease (probably transports guanosine, adenosine, 2'-deoxyguanosine, inosine and xanthosine with decreasing affinity in this order) ( Deka et al ., 2006 )

3.A.1.2.11.name: The erythritol permease, EryEFG (probably orthologous to 3.A.1.2.16)
3.A.1.2.11.description: The erythritol permease, EryEFG ( Geddes et al. , 2010 ) (probably orthologous to 3.A.1.2.16)

3.A.1.2.12.name: The (deoxy)ribonucleoside permease; probably takes up all deoxy- and ribonucleosides (cytidine, uridine, adenosine and toxic analogues…
3.A.1.2.12.description: The (deoxy)ribonucleoside permease; probably takes up all deoxy- and ribonucleosides (cytidine, uridine, adenosine and toxic analogues, fluorocytidine and fluorouridine tested), but not ribose or nucleobases ( Webb and Hosie, 2006 )

3.A.1.2.13.name: The probable autoinducer-2 (AI-2;, a furanosyl borate diester: 3aS,6S,6aR)- 2 , 2 ,6,6a-tetrahydroxy-3a-methyltetrahydrofuro[3, 2 -d][1,3, 2…
3.A.1.2.13.description: The probable autoinducer-2 (AI-2;, a furanosyl borate diester: 3aS,6S,6aR)- 2 , 2 ,6,6a-tetrahydroxy-3a-methyltetrahydrofuro[3, 2 -d][1,3, 2 ]dioxaborolan- 2 -uide) uptake porter ( Shao et al ., 2007 ) (50-70% identical to RbsABC of E. coli ; TC# 3.A.1.2.1)

3.A.1.2.14.name: Putative L-arabinose porter.
3.A.1.2.14.description: Putative L-arabinose porter ( Rodionov et al. 2010 ).

3.A.1.2.15.name: The putative xylitol uptake porter, XltABC
3.A.1.2.15.description: The putative xylitol uptake porter, XltABC ( Rodionov et al. , 2010 )

3.A.1.2.16.name: The erythritol uptake permease, EryEFG (probably orthologous to 3.A.1.2.11)
3.A.1.2.16.description: The erythritol uptake permease, EryEFG ( Yost et al. , 2006 ) (probably orthologous to 3.A.1.2.11)

3.A.1.2.17.name: General nucleoside uptake porter, NupABC/BmpA (transports all common nucleosides as well as 5-fluorocytidine, inosine, deoxyuridine and xanthosine)…
3.A.1.2.17.description: General nucleoside uptake porter, NupABC/BmpA (transports all common nucleosides as well as 5-fluorocytidine, inosine, deoxyuridine and xanthosine) ( Martinussen et al. , 2010 ) (Most similar to 3.A.1.2.12). NupA is 506aas with two ABC (C) domains. NupB has 8 predicted TMSs, NupC has 9 or 10 predicted TMSs in a 4 + 1 (or 2) + 4 arrangement.

3.A.1.2.18.name: Xylose porter.
3.A.1.2.18.description: Xylose porter ( Nanavati et al. 2006 ). Regulated by xylose-responsive regulator XylR ( Kazanov et al. , 2012 ).

3.A.1.2.19.name: D-ribose porter.
3.A.1.2.19.description: D-ribose porter ( Nanavati et al. , 2006 ). Induced by ribose ( Conners et al. , 2005 ).

3.A.1.2.20.name: Glucose porter.
3.A.1.2.20.description: Glucose porter. Also bind xylose ( Boucher and Noll 2011 ). Induced by glucose ( Frock et al. 2012 ). Directly regulated by glucose-responsive regulator GluR ( Kazanov et al. , 2012 ).

3.A.1.2.21.name: The myoinositol (high affinity)/ D-ribose (low affinity) transporter IatP/IatA/IbpA.
3.A.1.2.21.description: The myoinositol (high affinity)/ D-ribose (low affinity) transporter IatP/IatA/IbpA. The structure of IbpA with myoinositol bound has been solved ( Herrou and Crosson 2013 ).

3.A.1.2.24.name: XylFGH downstream of characterized transcriptional regulator, ROK7B7 (Sco6008); XylF (Sco6009); XylG (Sco6010); XylH (Sco6011)).
3.A.1.2.24.description: XylFGH downstream of characterized transcriptional regulator, ROK7B7 (Sco6008); XylF (Sco6009); XylG (Sco6010); XylH (Sco6011)) ( Świątek et al. 2013 ).

3.A.1.2.26.name: Xylose transporter, XylFGH (XylF (R), 359 aas; XylG (C), 525 aas; XylH (M), 389 aas.
3.A.1.2.26.description: Xylose transporter, XylFGH (XylF (R), 359 aas; XylG (C), 525 aas; XylH (M), 389 aas. Controlled by a 3 component sensor kinase/response regulator system (XylFII, sensor, A6LW07; LytS, SK, A6LW08; YesN, RR, A6LW09) ( Sun et al. 2015 ). The XylFII-LytS complex provides the molecular basis for D-xylose utilization and metabolic modification ( Li et al. 2017 ).

3.A.1.2.29.name: High affinity fructose uptake porter, FrtABC, Km (fructose) = ~100μM; expression of the frtABC operon is regulated by the product of the upstream…
3.A.1.2.29.description: High affinity fructose uptake porter, FrtABC, Km (fructose) = ~100μM; expression of the frtABC operon is regulated by the product of the upstream gene, frtR , FrtR, a LacI/GalR-type repressor that allows activation in the presence of fructose ( Ungerer et al. 2008 ). When FruR is eliminated, the cells become hypersensitive to fructose, and the level of fruABC expression is much higher than in the…

3.A.1.2.31.name: Putative purine porter with 4 components.
3.A.1.2.31.description: Putative purine porter with 4 components ( Chandravanshi et al. 2019 ).

3.A.1.2.32.name: ABC-type putative arabinose transport system, AraEGHP.
3.A.1.2.32.description: ABC-type putative arabinose transport system, AraEGHP. The genes encoding this system are found within a large gene cluster including many arabinose/pentose metabolic enzymes, a sensor kinase/response regulator pair, and an ABC uptake system specific for araino-oligosaccharides of 2 to 8 sugar units (TC# 3.A.1.1.57) ( Lansky et al. 2020 ).

3.A.1.2.33.name: XylFGH of T. ethanolicus.
3.A.1.2.33.description: XylFGH of T. ethanolicus ( Erbeznik et al. 2004 ).

3.A.1.2.6.name: D-allose porter.
3.A.1.2.6.description: D-allose porter. The structure of AlsB has been solved at 1.8 Å resolution ( Chaudhuri et al. 1999 ). Ten residues from both the domains form 14 hydrogen bonds with the sugar. 6-Deoxy-allose, 3-deoxy-glucose and ribose bind with reduced affinity so AlbP can function as a low affinity transporter for D-ribose ( Chaudhuri et al. 1999 ).

3.A.1.2.9.name: Rhamnose porter (Transport activity is dependent on rhamnokinase (RhaK; AAQ92412) activity This could be an example of group translocation!)
3.A.1.2.9.description: Rhamnose porter ( Richardson et al ., 2004 ) (Transport activity is dependent on rhamnokinase (RhaK; AAQ92412) activity ( Richardson and Oresnik, 2007 ) This could be an example of group translocation!)

3.A.1.20.name: The Brachyspira Iron Transporter (BIT) Family (Most similar to 3.A.1.6, 3.A.1.8 and 3.A.1.11)

3.A.1.20.1.name: The iron transporter, BitABCDEF.
3.A.1.20.1.description: The iron transporter, BitABCDEF ( Dugourd et al. 1999 ).

3.A.1.20.2.name: Hexose-phosphate transporter.
3.A.1.20.2.description: Hexose-phosphate transporter. Transports glucose-6-phosphate (Km = 0.3 υM) and fructose-6-phosphate (1.3 υM). Sugar phsophates can be used as both carbon and phosphate sources ( Moisi et al. 2013 ).

3.A.1.20.3.name: Iron (Fe 3+ ) uptake porter, AfuABC (FbpABC).
3.A.1.20.3.description: Iron (Fe 3+ ) uptake porter, AfuABC (FbpABC) ( Chin et al. 1996 ). AfuA has been characterized ( Willemsen et al. 1997 ).

3.A.1.20.5.name: A Mg 2+ -citrate uptake porter with three components, R, M and C, as suggested by Mandal et al. 2019.
3.A.1.20.5.description: A Mg 2+ -citrate uptake porter with three components, R, M and C, as suggested by Mandal et al. 2019 . This system alao be a ferric iron uptake system, based on sequence similarity studies (see other members of TC sub-family 3.A.1.20). The substrate binding protein, MctA, of the system, has been studied with and without Mg-citrate, and the 3-D structure at up to 1.63 Å resolution, indicating that…

3.A.1.201.17.name: Mitochondrial ABCB10 or ABC-me transporter.
3.A.1.201.17.description: Mitochondrial ABCB10 or ABC-me transporter. It is a mitochondrial inner membrane erythroid transporter involved in heme biosynthesis. ABCB10 possesses an unusually long 105-amino acid mitochondrial targeting presequence, the central subdomain of which (aas 36-70) is sufficient for mitochondrial import ( Graf et al. 2004 ) and is essential for erythropoiesis and protection of mitochondria against…

3.A.1.201.22.name: Mitochondrial ATP-binding cassette 1, ABCB8.
3.A.1.201.22.description: Mitochondrial ATP-binding cassette 1, ABCB8. Mediates doxorubicin resistance in melanoma cells ( Elliott and Al-Hajj 2009) . It is regulated by the Sp1 transcription factor and down regulated by mthramycin A which blocks Sp1 binding to the DNA ( Sachrajda and Ratajewski 2011 ). It is also regulated by neuropilin-1, NRP1 (TC# 8.A.47.1.5) ( Issitt et al. 2018 ). The cryo-EM structure of ABCB8 bound…

3.A.1.201.30.name: ABCB10 transporter of 655 aas and 6 TMSs in a domain arrangement of M-C. It functions in resistance to acaricides.
3.A.1.201.30.description: ABCB10 transporter of 655 aas and 6 TMSs in a domain arrangement of M-C. It functions in resistance to acaricides ( Koh-Tan et al. 2016 ). Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of AbcB10 causes cardiac dysfunction via lysosomal-mediated ferroptosis ( Do et al. 2024 ). AbcB10 knockout cardiomyocytes exhibit increased ROS production, iron accumulation, and lysosomal hypertrophy ( Do et al. 2024 ). The…

3.A.1.201.8.name: The aluminum chelate (aluminum sensitivity (ALS1)) protein; expressed in root vacuoles half-type ABC transporter.
3.A.1.201.8.description: The aluminum chelate (aluminum sensitivity (ALS1)) protein; expressed in root vacuoles half-type ABC transporter (not induced by aluminum; Larsen et al ., 2007 ).

3.A.1.203.name: The Peroxysomal Fatty Acyl CoA Transporter (P-FAT) Family (ABCD)

3.A.1.203.11.name: Putative fatty acid exporter; homodimer.
3.A.1.203.11.description: Putative fatty acid exporter; homodimer ( Moussatova et al. 2008 ).

3.A.1.203.12.name: ABC transporter, BclA, of 586 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 arrangement in the N-terminus and the ABC domain in the C-terminus.
3.A.1.203.12.description: ABC transporter, BclA, of 586 aas and 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 arrangement in the N-terminus and the ABC domain in the C-terminus. It is a peptide transprter required for bacteroid differentiation. It catalyzes import of peptides called nodule-specific cysteine-rich (NCR) peptides in the symbiotic nodule cells which house the bacteroids. NCR peptides are related to antimicrobial peptides of innate…

3.A.1.203.4.name: The BacA (Rv1819c) porter (selective for the uptake of bleomycin and antimicrobial peptides) (essential for maintenance of extended chronic…
3.A.1.203.4.description: The BacA (Rv1819c) porter (selective for the uptake of bleomycin and antimicrobial peptides) (essential for maintenance of extended chronic infection) ( Domenech et al. , 2009 ).

3.A.1.203.8.name: Peroxisomal/chloroplast fatty acyl CoA transporter, ABCD2.
3.A.1.203.8.description: Peroxisomal/chloroplast fatty acyl CoA transporter, ABCD2 ( Linka and Esser 2012 ).

3.A.1.21.1.name: The Fe 3+ -Yersiniabactin uptake transporter, YbtPQ.
3.A.1.21.1.description: The Fe 3+ -Yersiniabactin uptake transporter, YbtPQ ( Brem et al ., 2001 ; Fetherston et al ., 1999 ). YbtPQ is a virulence factor in the highly inflammatory microenvironment characteristic of high-titer cystitis in E. coli ( Koh et al. 2016 ). The E. coli and Y. pestis YbtP proteins are 99.7% identical. Multiple structures of the yersiniabactin importer YbtPQ from uropathogenic Escherichia coli…

3.A.1.21.2.name: The Fe 3+ -mycobactin/carboxymycobactin transporter, IrtAB.
3.A.1.21.2.description: The Fe 3+ -mycobactin/carboxymycobactin transporter, IrtAB ( Rodriguez and Smith, 2006 ). IrtA contains an FAD-binding domain ( Ryndak et al. , 2010 ). M. tuberculosis produces two classes of siderophores, lipid-bound mycobactin and water-soluble carboxymycobactin. Iron-loaded carboxymycobactin is imported into the cytoplasm by IrtAB which has an additional cytoplasmic siderophore interaction…

3.A.1.210.15.name: ABC exporter, ABCB7; PexA; Atm1, of 612 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs with an ATPase domain C-terminal (M-C), probably specific for polysulfides, being…
3.A.1.210.15.description: ABC exporter, ABCB7; PexA; Atm1, of 612 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs with an ATPase domain C-terminal (M-C), probably specific for polysulfides, being exported from the cytooplasm to the periplasm. I is 47% identical to PexA (ABCB7) of humans ( Riedel et al. 2019 ).

3.A.1.210.16.name: ABC transporter permease (residues 1 - 290) with ATP-binding protein (residues 291 - 583) of 583 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS…
3.A.1.210.16.description: ABC transporter permease (residues 1 - 290) with ATP-binding protein (residues 291 - 583) of 583 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

3.A.1.210.17.name: ABC transporter permease (residues 1 - 310) with ATP-binding protein (residues 311 - 593) of 593 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS…
3.A.1.210.17.description: ABC transporter permease (residues 1 - 310) with ATP-binding protein (residues 311 - 593) of 593 aas and 6 N-terminal TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

3.A.1.210.9.name: The Ni 2+ /Co 2+ exporter AtmA.
3.A.1.210.9.description: The Ni 2+ /Co 2+ exporter AtmA. Repressed by Zn 2+ , but not induced by Ni 2+ or Co 2+ ( Mikolay and Nies, 2009 ).

3.A.1.211.24.name: ABCF3 or ABC50 of 712 aas and 0 TMSs.
3.A.1.211.24.description: ABCF3 or ABC50 of 712 aas and 0 TMSs. ABC50 plays a key role in translation initiation and has functions that are distinct from those of other non-membrane ABC proteins ( Paytubi et al. 2009 ).

3.A.1.211.25.name: ABC protein, OptrA, of 619 aas and 0 TMSs, having the domain order of C-C. It is not involved in the export of drugs (oxazolidinones and…
3.A.1.211.25.description: ABC protein, OptrA, of 619 aas and 0 TMSs, having the domain order of C-C. It is not involved in the export of drugs (oxazolidinones and phenicols)out of the cell and may confer ribosomal protection ( Wang et al. 2018 ). .

3.A.1.212.1.name: The mitochondrial peptide exporter, Mdl1p (exports peptides of 6-21 amino acyl residues from the mitochondrial matrix as well as degradation products…
3.A.1.212.1.description: The mitochondrial peptide exporter, Mdl1p (exports peptides of 6-21 amino acyl residues from the mitochondrial matrix as well as degradation products of misassembled respiratory chain complexes) ( Janas et al ., 2003 ; van der Does et al ., 2006 ; Gompf et al ., 2007 ). A leaderless Mdl1p targets to the ER membrane instead of to the mitochondria ( Gompf et al ., 2007 ).

3.A.1.22.2.name: The ABC exporter, CbiMNQ 1 O 1.
3.A.1.22.2.description: The ABC exporter, CbiMNQ 1 O 1. CbiM and CbiQ1 both have 6 TMSs in a 2 + 2 + 2 TMS arrangement.

3.A.1.23.2.name: Putative cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter
3.A.1.23.2.description: Putative cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter ( Chen and Burne, 2003 )

3.A.1.23.5.name: Putative Ni 2+ /Co 2+ uptake porter, NikMNOQ.
3.A.1.23.5.description: Putative Ni 2+ /Co 2+ uptake porter, NikMNOQ ( Yu et al. 2013 ).

3.A.1.23.6.name: Cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter.
3.A.1.23.6.description: Cobalt (Co 2+ ) porter ( Rodionov et al ., 2006). CbiMN is a bipartite S-subunit with 8 TMSs ( Siche et al. 2010 ). Dynamic interactions of CbiN and CbiM trigger activity of the transporter ( Finkenwirth et al. 2019 ). Substrate binding (S) components rotate within the membrane to expose their binding pockets alternately to the exterior and the cytoplasm. In contrast to vitamin transporters…

3.A.1.23.7.name: Ni 2+ , Co 2+ uptake transporter, NikMNOQ (subunit sizes: NikMN, 347 aas, 9 TMSs; NikQ, 284 aas, 4 TMSs; NikO, 254 aas, 0 TMS.
3.A.1.23.7.description: Ni 2+ , Co 2+ uptake transporter, NikMNOQ (subunit sizes: NikMN, 347 aas, 9 TMSs; NikQ, 284 aas, 4 TMSs; NikO, 254 aas, 0 TMS. NikMN can take up Ni 2+ without NikQ or NikO ( Kirsch and Eitinger 2014 ).

3.A.1.23.8.name: Ni 2+ /Co 2+ uptake porter, CbiMNOQ (CbiM, 222 aas, 5 TMSs; CbiN, 103 aas, 2 TMSs; CbiO, 280 aas, 0 TMSs; CbiQ, 244 aas, 5 TMSs).
3.A.1.23.8.description: Ni 2+ /Co 2+ uptake porter, CbiMNOQ (CbiM, 222 aas, 5 TMSs; CbiN, 103 aas, 2 TMSs; CbiO, 280 aas, 0 TMSs; CbiQ, 244 aas, 5 TMSs). CbiMN can take up Ni 2+ without CbiO or CbiQ ( Kirsch and Eitinger 2014 ).

3.A.1.24.name: The Methionine Uptake Transporter (MUT) Family (Similar to 3.A.1.3 and 3.A.1.12)

3.A.1.24.5.name: L-Histidine uptake porter, MetIQN
3.A.1.24.5.description: L-Histidine uptake porter, MetIQN ( Johnson et al. 2008 )

3.A.1.25.5.name: Biotin/Riboflavin ECF transport system, EcfAA'T/RibU/BioY.
3.A.1.25.5.description: Biotin/Riboflavin ECF transport system, EcfAA'T/RibU/BioY ( Karpowich and Wang 2013 ). RibU binds riboflavin with high affinity, and the protein-substrate complex is exceptionally stable in solution. The crystal structure of riboflavin-bound RibU reveals an electronegative binding pocket at the extracellular surface in which the substrate is completely buried ( Karpowich et al. 2016 ).

3.A.1.25.6.name: Riboflavin ECF transport system, EcfAA'T/RibU.
3.A.1.25.6.description: Riboflavin ECF transport system, EcfAA'T/RibU ( Karpowich and Wang 2013 ).

3.A.1.25.8.name: An ECF ABC transporter with 4 subunits, EcfS/EcfT/EcfA/EcfA'.
3.A.1.25.8.description: An ECF ABC transporter with 4 subunits, EcfS/EcfT/EcfA/EcfA'. EcfS is also called RibU; EcfT is also called CbiQ, EcfA is also called Cbi01, and EcfA' is also called Cbi02. This system can take up riboflavin and possibly other vitamins ( Karpowich et al. 2015 ). ATP binding to the EcfAA' ATPases drives a conformational change that dissociates the S subunit from the EcfAA'T ECF module. Upon…

3.A.1.26.10.name: ATP-dependent folic acid uptake porter, FolT/EcfT/EcfA1/EcfA2.
3.A.1.26.10.description: ATP-dependent folic acid uptake porter, FolT/EcfT/EcfA1/EcfA2. The crystal structure of FolT has been solved to 3.2 Å resolution in substrate-bound and free conformations, revealing a potential gating mechanism ( Zhao et al. 2015 ).

3.A.1.26.11.name: Putative pantothenate uptake porter, PanT/EcfA/EcfA'/EcfT.
3.A.1.26.11.description: Putative pantothenate uptake porter, PanT/EcfA/EcfA'/EcfT ( Rodionova et al. 2015 ).

3.A.1.26.12.name: Chloroplast heavy metal ion uptake porter with at least two components, ABCI10, 271 aas (C) and ABCI12, 391 aas (M), present in the inner chloroplast…
3.A.1.26.12.description: Chloroplast heavy metal ion uptake porter with at least two components, ABCI10, 271 aas (C) and ABCI12, 391 aas (M), present in the inner chloroplast envelope. Loss of ABCI10 and ABCI11 gene products in Arabidopsis leads to dwarfed, albino plants showing impaired chloroplast biogenesis and deregulated metal homeostasis. The membrane-intrinsic protein ABCI12 may be the interaction partner for…

3.A.1.26.5.name: ThiW/CbiQ/CbiO homologues (ThiW: 174 aas; 5 putative TMSs).
3.A.1.26.5.description: ThiW/CbiQ/CbiO homologues (ThiW: 174 aas; 5 putative TMSs). Possible thiamin uptake porter ( Rodionov et al. , 2009 ).

3.A.1.26.7.name: The putative hydroxyethyl thiazole (biosynthetic precursor of thiamine) porter, ThiW-EcfA1-A2-EcfT (this is a group II ECF transporter which uses a…
3.A.1.26.7.description: The putative hydroxyethyl thiazole (biosynthetic precursor of thiamine) porter, ThiW-EcfA1-A2-EcfT (this is a group II ECF transporter which uses a universal energy-coupling module (EcfA1-EcfA2-EcfT) in many firmicutes; Rodionov et al. , 2002 ).

3.A.1.26.9.name: The folate transporter, FolT/EcfAA''T (The 3-d structure is known to 3.0Å resolution.
3.A.1.26.9.description: The folate transporter, FolT/EcfAA''T (The 3-d structure is known to 3.0Å resolution ( Xu et al. 2013 ; 4HUQ). This transporter uses the same ECF energy coupling complex (AA''T) as 3.A.1.28.2.

3.A.1.27.1.name: The γ-hexachlorocyclohexane (γHCH) uptake permease, LinKLMN (most similar to 3.A.1.12.4, the QAT family)
3.A.1.27.1.description: The γ-hexachlorocyclohexane (γHCH) uptake permease, LinKLMN (most similar to 3.A.1.12.4, the QAT family) ( Endo et al ., 2007 )

3.A.1.27.2.name: The chloroplast lipid (trigalactosyl diacyl glycerol (TDG)) transporter, Tdg1,2,3.
3.A.1.27.2.description: The chloroplast lipid (trigalactosyl diacyl glycerol (TDG)) transporter, Tdg1,2,3 ( Lu et al ., 2007 ). Lipids such as mono- and digalactolipids are synthesized in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) of plant cells and transferred to the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts. Mutations in an outer chloroplastic envelope protein with 350 aas and 7 putative TMSs in the last 250 residues may catalyze…

3.A.1.27.3.name: ABC transporter maintaining outer membrane (OM) lipid asymmetry, MlaABCDEF (YrbABCDEF).
3.A.1.27.3.description: ABC transporter maintaining outer membrane (OM) lipid asymmetry, MlaABCDEF (YrbABCDEF) ( Malinverni and Silhavy, 2009 ). MlaA (VacJ) is a "spreading" protein, essential for Shigella pathogenicity ( Suzuki et al. , 1994 ). The ABC transporter, MlaEFBD, provides energy for maintaining OM lipid asymmetry via the transport of aberrantly localized phospholipids (PLs) from the OM to the inner membrane…

3.A.1.27.4.name: The cholesterol uptake porter.
3.A.1.27.4.description: The cholesterol uptake porter ( Mohn et al. , 2008 ). Takes up cholesterol, 5-α-cholestanol, 5-α-cholestanone, β-sitosterol, etc. (It is not established that all of these proteins comprise the system or that other gene products are not involved.)

3.A.1.27.5.name: The Mce/Yrb/Mlk (Mammalian cell entry) ABC-type putative steroid uptake transporter (involved in several aspects of mycobacterial pathogenesis).
3.A.1.27.5.description: The Mce/Yrb/Mlk (Mammalian cell entry) ABC-type putative steroid uptake transporter (involved in several aspects of mycobacterial pathogenesis) ( Mohn et al. , 2008 ; Joshi et al. , 2006 ).

3.A.1.28.2.name: The folate transporter, FolT/EcfAA''T (The 3-d structure is known to 3.0Å resolution.
3.A.1.28.2.description: The folate transporter, FolT/EcfAA''T (The 3-d structure is known to 3.0Å resolution ( Xu et al. 2013 ; 4HUQ). Thiamine and riboflavin may also be substrates.

3.A.1.3.name: The Polar Amino Acid Uptake Transporter (PAAT) Family

3.A.1.3.1.name: Histidine/arginine/lysine/ornithine porter.
3.A.1.3.1.description: Histidine/arginine/lysine/ornithine porter ( Heuveling et al. 2014 ). In contrast to some homologous homodimeric systems, the heterodimeric histidine transporter of Salmonella enterica Typhimurium ligands only one substrate molecule in between its two transmembrane subunits, HisM and HisQ ( Heuveling et al. 2019 ).

3.A.1.3.10.name: Cystine/cysteine/diaminopimelate transporter, CysXYZ; these proteins are also designated FliY/YecS/YecC.
3.A.1.3.10.description: Cystine/cysteine/diaminopimelate transporter, CysXYZ; these proteins are also designated FliY/YecS/YecC. Note, another transporter is designated CysZ in E. coli (TC# 2.A.121.1.1). CysXYZ also transports the toxic amino acid analogues, L-selenaproline (SCA; L-selenazolidine-4-carboxylic acid) and L-selenocystine (SeCys) ( Deutch et al. 2014 ). FliY binds L-cystine, L-cysteine, and D-cysteine with…

3.A.1.3.11.name: Arginine/ornithine (but not lysine) porter.
3.A.1.3.11.description: Arginine/ornithine (but not lysine) porter ( Nishijyo et al. 1998 ).

3.A.1.3.13.name: Uptake system for L-cystine (Km=2.5 μM), L-cystathionine, L-djenkolate ( 2-amino-3-[(2-amino-3-hydroxy-3-oxopropyl)sulfanylmethylsulfanyl] propanoic…
3.A.1.3.13.description: Uptake system for L-cystine (Km=2.5 μM), L-cystathionine, L-djenkolate ( 2-amino-3-[(2-amino-3-hydroxy-3-oxopropyl)sulfanylmethylsulfanyl] propanoic acid), and S-methyl-L-cysteine ( Burguière et al. , 2004 , Burguière et al. , 2005 )

3.A.1.3.14.name: Uptake system for L-cystine
3.A.1.3.14.description: Uptake system for L-cystine ( Burguière et al. , 2004 )

3.A.1.3.15.name: Putative uptake system for arginine, YqiXYZ
3.A.1.3.15.description: Putative uptake system for arginine, YqiXYZ ( Sekowska et al. , 2001 )

3.A.1.3.16.name: Uptake system for glutamate and aspartate.
3.A.1.3.16.description: Uptake system for glutamate and aspartate ( Leon-Kempis et al ., 2006 ). This four component system appears to be important for pathogenicity ( Gao et al. 2017 ).

3.A.1.3.17.name: Basic amino acid uptake transporter, BgtAB
3.A.1.3.17.description: Basic amino acid uptake transporter, BgtAB (BgtA is shared with NatFGH/BgtA; 3.A.1.3.18; Pernil et al ., 2008 )

3.A.1.3.18.name: Acidic and neutral amino acid uptake transporter NatFGH/BgtA.
3.A.1.3.18.description: Acidic and neutral amino acid uptake transporter NatFGH/BgtA. BgtA is shared with BgtAB (3.A.1.3.17; Pernil et al ., 2008 )

3.A.1.3.19.name: Acidic amino acid uptake porter, AatJMQP.
3.A.1.3.19.description: Acidic amino acid uptake porter, AatJMQP ( Singh and Röhm, 2008 ). It is the sole system that transports glutamate and glutamine, but it can also transport aspartate and asparagine ( Singh and Röhm 2008 ).

3.A.1.3.2.name: Three component ABC L-glutamine porter.
3.A.1.3.2.description: Three component ABC L-glutamine porter. The basal ATPase activity (ATP hydrolysis in the absence of substrate) is mainly caused by the docking of the closed-unliganded state of GlnH onto the transporter domain of GlnPQ. Unlike glutamine, arginine binds both GlnH domains, but does not trigger their closing. Comparison of the ATPase activity in nanodiscs with glutamine transport in proteoliposomes…

3.A.1.3.20.name: The putative lysine uptake system, LysXY
3.A.1.3.20.description: The putative lysine uptake system, LysXY

3.A.1.3.21.name: Hydroxy L-proline uptake porter, HprABC.
3.A.1.3.21.description: Hydroxy L-proline uptake porter, HprABC ( Johnson et al. 2008 ).

3.A.1.3.22.name: Amino acid transporter, AatJMQP.
3.A.1.3.22.description: Amino acid transporter, AatJMQP. Probably transports L-glutamate, D-glutamate, L-glutamine and N-acetyl L-glutamate ( Johnson et al. 2008 ). Very similar to 3.A.1.3.19 of P. putida

3.A.1.3.23.name: Amino acid transporter, PA5152-PA5155.
3.A.1.3.23.description: Amino acid transporter, PA5152-PA5155. Probably transports numerous amino acids including lysine, arginine, histidine, D-alanine and D-valine ( Johnson et al. 2008 ). Regulated by ArgR.

3.A.1.3.24.name: Putative methionine uptake porter, Sco_5260, 5259, 5258.
3.A.1.3.24.description: Putative methionine uptake porter, Sco_5260, 5259, 5258. Defects cause impaired sporulation, reduced growth and reduced production of actinorhodin and undecylprodigiosin. Induced by S-adenosylmethionine ( Shin et al. 2007 ).

3.A.1.3.25.name: Glutamine transporter, GlnQP.
3.A.1.3.25.description: Glutamine transporter, GlnQP. Takes up glutamine, asparagine and glutamate which compete for each other for binding to the substrate/transmembrane protein constituent of the system ( Fulyani et al. 2015 ). Tandem substrate binding domains differ in substrate specificity and affinity, allowing cells to efficiently accumulate different amino acids via a single ABC transporter. Analysis revealed the…

3.A.1.3.26.name: The putative polar amino acid uptake porter, YhdWXYZ.
3.A.1.3.26.description: The putative polar amino acid uptake porter, YhdWXYZ. Probably under NtrBC transcriptional control ( Jiang et al. 2006 ).

3.A.1.3.27.name: Basic amino acid uptake porter, ArtIQ 2 N 2.
3.A.1.3.27.description: Basic amino acid uptake porter, ArtIQ 2 N 2. Transports Arginine, lysine and histidine. Several 3-d structures have been solved (4YMS, 4YMT, 4YMU, etc., Yu et al. 2015 ). These revealed one binding site for substrate per ArtQ monomer. Heuveling et al. 2018 then showed that in the close homologue, ArtMP of Geobacillus stearothermophilus, that just one of these two sites needed to bind substrate to…

3.A.1.3.28.name: Putative amino acid uptake porter, YckIJK; deletion of YckK (substrate binding protein) increases sensitivity to the antimicrobial peptide, cecropin.
3.A.1.3.28.description: Putative amino acid uptake porter, YckIJK; deletion of YckK (substrate binding protein) increases sensitivity to the antimicrobial peptide, cecropin ( Chen et al. 2015 ).

3.A.1.3.29.name: Histidine/Arginine/Lysine (basic amino acid) uptake porter, HisJ/ArgT/HisP/HisM/HisQ [R, R, C, M, M, respectively].
3.A.1.3.29.description: Histidine/Arginine/Lysine (basic amino acid) uptake porter, HisJ/ArgT/HisP/HisM/HisQ [R, R, C, M, M, respectively] ( Gilson et al. 1982 ). HisJ binds L-His (preferred), but 1-methyl-L-His and 3-methyl-L-His also bind, while the dipeptide carnosine binds weakly; D-histidine and the histidine degradation products, histamine, urocanic acid and imidazole do not bind. L-Arg, homo-L-Arg, and…

3.A.1.3.30.name: Putative ABC amino acid uptake porter with 3 constituents.
3.A.1.3.30.description: Putative ABC amino acid uptake porter with 3 constituents. The membrane protein is different from other members of this subfamily in having 10 TMSs in a 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 TMS arrangement with a probable 5 TMS duplication), and the receptor has two TMSs at the N- and C-termini.

3.A.1.3.4.name: Glutamate/aspartate porter.
3.A.1.3.4.description: Glutamate/aspartate porter. Similar in sequence to 3.A.1.3.19 which is specific for Glu, Asp, Gln and Asn ( Singh and Röhm 2008 ).

3.A.1.3.8.name: General L-amino acid porter; transports basic and acidic amino acids preferentially, but also transports aliphatic amino acids (catalyzes both uptake…
3.A.1.3.8.description: General L-amino acid porter; transports basic and acidic amino acids preferentially, but also transports aliphatic amino acids (catalyzes both uptake and efflux) ( Prell et al. 2009; Hosie et al. 2002 Hosie et al. 2002 ).

3.A.1.30.1.name: The putative thiamin precursor uptake transporter, YkoEDC (E is most similar to 3.A.1.4.3; D is most similar to 3.A.1.26.2; C is most similar to…
3.A.1.30.1.description: The putative thiamin precursor uptake transporter, YkoEDC ( Rodionov et al. , 2009 ) (E is most similar to 3.A.1.4.3; D is most similar to 3.A.1.26.2; C is most similar to 3.A.1.23.2).

3.A.1.34.1.name: The putative tryptophan uptake transporter, TrpXYZ.
3.A.1.34.1.description: The putative tryptophan uptake transporter, TrpXYZ. Regulated by tryptophan-specific T-box ( Vitreschak et al. 2008 )

3.A.1.4.name: The Hydrophobic Amino Acid Uptake Transporter (HAAT) Family

3.A.1.4.1.name: Leucine; leucine/isoleucine/valine porter
3.A.1.4.1.description: Leucine; leucine/isoleucine/valine porter (also transports phenylalanine and tyrosine; Koyanagi et al ., 2004 )

3.A.1.4.10.name: The branched chain hydrophobic amino acid transporter, LivJFGHM.
3.A.1.4.10.description: The branched chain hydrophobic amino acid transporter, LivJFGHM ( Basavanna et al. 2009 ).

3.A.1.4.11.name: The phenylpropeneoid uptake porter, CouPSTW.
3.A.1.4.11.description: The phenylpropeneoid uptake porter, CouPSTW. The purple photosynthetic bacterium Rhodopseudomonas palustris is able to grow photoheterotrophically under anaerobic conditions on a range of phenylpropeneoid lignin monomers, including coumarate, ferulate, caffeate, and cinnamate. RPA1789 (CouP) is the periplasmic binding-protein component of the ABC uptake system (CouPSTU). CouP binds a range of…

3.A.1.4.12.name: ABC-type uptake porter for pyruvate and monocarboxylate 2-oxo acids.
3.A.1.4.12.description: ABC-type uptake porter for pyruvate and monocarboxylate 2-oxo acids. Pyruvate uptake has been measured and is inhibited by monocarboxylate 2-oxo-acids such as 2-oxobutyrate, 2-oxovalerate, 2-oxoisovalerate, 2-oxoisocaproate and 2-oxo 3-methylvalerate which are probably substrates ( Pernil et al. 2010 ).

3.A.1.4.14.name: Branched chain amino acid uptake (BCAA) porter consisting of 5 proteins.
3.A.1.4.14.description: Branched chain amino acid uptake (BCAA) porter consisting of 5 proteins.

3.A.1.4.15.name: ABC transporter for benzoate and phenyl proponoids with 6 subunits, one receptor (R) for benzoate and one receptor (R) for phenyl proponoids derived…
3.A.1.4.15.description: ABC transporter for benzoate and phenyl proponoids with 6 subunits, one receptor (R) for benzoate and one receptor (R) for phenyl proponoids derived from plant lignins. There are also two membrane constituents (M) and two cytoplasmic ATPases (C) (see proteins for this system) ( Vagts et al. 2021 ).

3.A.1.4.3.name: General L- (and D-)amino acid uptake porter (transports acidic, basic, polar, semipolar and hydrophobic amino acids).
3.A.1.4.3.description: General L- (and D-)amino acid uptake porter (transports acidic, basic, polar, semipolar and hydrophobic amino acids). The amino and carboxyl groups do not need to be α since γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is a substrate. The system may function with additional binding proteins since L-alanine uptake is not dependent on BraC.

3.A.1.4.5.name: The high affinity urea/thiourea/hydroxyurea porter
3.A.1.4.5.description: The high affinity urea/thiourea/hydroxyurea porter ( Beckers et al ., 2004 )

3.A.1.4.6.name: The neutral amino acid permease, N-1 (transports pro, phe, leu, gly, ala, ser, gln and his, but gln and his are not transported via NatB)
3.A.1.4.6.description: The neutral amino acid permease, N-1 (transports pro, phe, leu, gly, ala, ser, gln and his, but gln and his are not transported via NatB) ( Picossi et al ., 2005 )

3.A.1.4.7.name: The protocatechuate (3,4-dihydroxybenzoate) uptake porter, PcaMNVWX
3.A.1.4.7.description: The protocatechuate (3,4-dihydroxybenzoate) uptake porter, PcaMNVWX ( Maclean et al. , 2011 )

3.A.1.4.8.name: Branched chain amino acid uptake transporter.
3.A.1.4.8.description: Branched chain amino acid uptake transporter. Transports alanine ( Hoshino and Kose 1990 ).

3.A.1.4.9.name: Uptake transporter, CamABCD of cholate (steroid) metabolites, 1β(2'-propanoate)-3aα-H-4α(3"(R)-hydroxy-3"-propanoate)-7aβ-methylhexahydro-5-indanone…
3.A.1.4.9.description: Uptake transporter, CamABCD of cholate (steroid) metabolites, 1β(2'-propanoate)-3aα-H-4α(3"(R)-hydroxy-3"-propanoate)-7aβ-methylhexahydro-5-indanone and a desaturated analog ( Swain et al. 2012 ).

3.A.1.5.1.name: Oligopeptide porter (also takes up amino glycoside antibiotics such as kanamycin, streptomycin and neomycin as well as cell wall-derived peptides…
3.A.1.5.1.description: Oligopeptide porter (also takes up amino glycoside antibiotics such as kanamycin, streptomycin and neomycin as well as cell wall-derived peptides such as murein tripeptide). It transports substrate peptides of 2-5 amino acids with highest affinity for tripeptides. Also transports δ-aminolevulinic acid (ALA). [May be regulated by PTS Enzyme I Ntr -aspartokinase.] ATP-binding to OppDF may result in…

3.A.1.5.11.name: Glutathione porter, YliABCD or GsiABCD.
3.A.1.5.11.description: Glutathione porter, YliABCD or GsiABCD ( Suzuki et al ., 2005 ). Changes in the redox balance in the medium and in E. coli cells affect the ability of bacteria to form biofilms. An increase in the level of aeration in the culture of wild-type bacteria led to a 3-fold decrease in the mass of biofilms ( Kalashnikova et al. 2023 ). Mutants lacking components of the glutathione and thioredoxin redox…

3.A.1.5.12.name: Probable rhamnose oligosaccharide porter.
3.A.1.5.12.description: Probable rhamnose oligosaccharide porter. Induced by rhamnose ( Conners et al ., 2005 ).

3.A.1.5.14.name: Probable cellobiose porter.
3.A.1.5.14.description: Probable cellobiose porter. Induced by barley, glucomannan ( Conners et al ., 2005 )

3.A.1.5.15.name: Probable mannose/mannoside porter.
3.A.1.5.15.description: Probable mannose/mannoside porter. Induced by beta-mannan ( Conners et al ., 2005 ). Regulated by mannose-responsive regulator manR ( Kazanov et al. , 2012 ).

3.A.1.5.17.name: The proline betaine uptake porter
3.A.1.5.17.description: The proline betaine uptake porter ( Alloing et al ., 2006 )

3.A.1.5.18.name: The oligopeptide transporter OppA1-5, B1, C1, DF (functions with five binding proteins of differing induction properties and peptide specificities…
3.A.1.5.18.description: The oligopeptide transporter OppA1-5, B1, C1, DF (functions with five binding proteins of differing induction properties and peptide specificities; OppA1-3 are chromosomally encoded; OppA4 and 5 are plasmid encoded.) ( Medrano et al ., 2007 )

3.A.1.5.19.name: The major oligopeptide uptake porter, Opp-3 (of four paralogues, this is the only one that mediates nitrogen nutrition.
3.A.1.5.19.description: The major oligopeptide uptake porter, Opp-3 (of four paralogues, this is the only one that mediates nitrogen nutrition ( Hiron et al ., 2007 ).

3.A.1.5.2.name: Dipeptide porter.
3.A.1.5.2.description: Dipeptide porter. Also transports δ-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and heme ( Létoffé et al. , 2008 ).

3.A.1.5.20.name: 5-6 amino acyl oligopeptide transporter AppA-F.
3.A.1.5.20.description: 5-6 amino acyl oligopeptide transporter AppA-F ( Koide and Hoch, 1994 ).

3.A.1.5.21.name: The Microcin C/peptide uptake porter, YejABEF.
3.A.1.5.21.description: The Microcin C/peptide uptake porter, YejABEF ( Novikova et al ., 2007 ). The 'Trojan horse' antibiotic, microcin C, consists of a nonhydrolyzable aspartyl-adenylate that is efficiently imported into bacterial cells owing to a covalently attached peptide. Once inside the cell, the peptide "carrier" is removed by proteolytic processing to release a potent aspartyl tRNA synthetase inhibitor (…

3.A.1.5.22.name: The peptide transporter OppA,B,C,D,F. Similar to 3.A.1.5.1, OppA is similar to the Vibrio furnissii OppA that provides several functions: hemolysis…
3.A.1.5.22.description: The peptide transporter OppA,B,C,D,F (influences biofilm formation; Lee et al ., 2004 ). Similar to 3.A.1.5.1, OppA is similar to the Vibrio furnissii OppA that provides several functions: hemolysis, antibiotic resistance, and virulence ( Wu et al ., 2007 ).

3.A.1.5.23.name: The Ethylene diamine tetraacetate (EDTA) uptake porter, EppABCD.
3.A.1.5.23.description: The Ethylene diamine tetraacetate (EDTA) uptake porter, EppABCD ( Zhang et al ., 2007 ).

3.A.1.5.24.name: The antimicrobial peptide (protamine, melittin, polymyxin B, human defensin (HBD)-1 and HBD-2 exporter, YejABEF.
3.A.1.5.24.description: The antimicrobial peptide (protamine, melittin, polymyxin B, human defensin (HBD)-1 and HBD-2 exporter, YejABEF ( Eswarappa et al. , 2008 ). Prefers N-formyl methionine peptides, such as Microcin C (of prokaryotic origin) to non formylated peptides (of eukaryotic origin) ( Novikova et al ., 2007 ).

3.A.1.5.25.name: The ABC peptide/signalling peptide transporter.
3.A.1.5.25.description: The ABC peptide/signalling peptide transporter. OptA binds peptides of 3-6 aas; OptS binds dipeptides. OptB,C,D are most similar to 3.A.1.5.19.

3.A.1.5.26.name: The glutathione transporter, OppA.
3.A.1.5.26.description: The glutathione transporter, OppA ( Dasgupta et al. , 2010 ). OppA binds glutathione and the nanopeptide, bradykinin. Also regulates cytokine release, apoptosis and the innate immune response of macrophages infected with M. tuberculosis ( Dasgupta et al. , 2010 ).

3.A.1.5.27.name: The glutathione uptake porter, DppBCDF with the glutathione binding protein, DppA (GbpA; HbpA).
3.A.1.5.27.description: The glutathione uptake porter, DppBCDF with the glutathione binding protein, DppA (GbpA; HbpA). Takes up reduced (GSH) and oxidized (GSSG) but not bulky glutathione S conjugates or glutathione derivatives with C-terminal modifications ( Vergauwen et al. , 2010 ).

3.A.1.5.28.name: The Nickel (Ni 2+ ) uptake porter, NikZYXWV.
3.A.1.5.28.description: The Nickel (Ni 2+ ) uptake porter, NikZYXWV ( Howlett et al. , 2012 ).

3.A.1.5.29.name: Probable xylan oligosaccharide porter.
3.A.1.5.29.description: Probable xylan oligosaccharide porter ( Conners et al. 2005 ). Induced by cylan and xylose. Regulated by xylose-responsive regulator XylR ( Kazanov et al. 2012 ).

3.A.1.5.3.name: Nickel porter.
3.A.1.5.3.description: Nickel porter. Histidine 416 of NikA is essential for nickel uptake ( Cavazza et al. , 2011 ).

3.A.1.5.33.name: The Nickel (Ni 2+ ) uptake porter, NikABCDE
3.A.1.5.33.description: The Nickel (Ni 2+ ) uptake porter, NikABCDE ( Hiron et al. 2010 )

3.A.1.5.34.name: Putative oligopeptide uptake porter.
3.A.1.5.34.description: Putative oligopeptide uptake porter. Induced by S-adenosylmethionine. Deletion caused impaired sporulation and impaired the enhancing activity of S-adenosylmethionine on actinorhodin (but not undecylprodigiosin) production ( Shin et al. 2007 ).

3.A.1.5.35.name: Putative peptide transporter encoded adjacent to the putative transport system with TC#3.A.1.5.36.
3.A.1.5.35.description: Putative peptide transporter encoded adjacent to the putative transport system with TC#3.A.1.5.36. The orthologue controls aerial mycelium formation in S. griseus ( Akanuma et al. 2011 ).

3.A.1.5.36.name: Peptide transporter encoded adjacent to the putative transport system with TC#3.A.1.5.35.
3.A.1.5.36.description: Peptide transporter encoded adjacent to the putative transport system with TC#3.A.1.5.35 ( Akanuma et al. 2011 ). Induced by exogenous S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) at a concentration of 2muM which also enhanced antibiotic production and inhibited morphological development ( Park et al. 2005 ). SAM can be imported into cells. Mutants in the bldK genes confer resistance to the toxic tripeptide…

3.A.1.5.37.name: The ABC BldKA-E (SGR_2418-2414) oligopeptide transport system.
3.A.1.5.37.description: The ABC BldKA-E (SGR_2418-2414) oligopeptide transport system. It controls aerial mycelium formation on glucose media. Probably involved in extracellular peptide signalling ( Akanuma et al. 2011 ). Probably orthologous to 3.A.1.5.35.

3.A.1.5.38.name: The putative D-alanyl-D-alanyl dipeptide permease, DdpABCDF; encoded within an operon that includes the D-ala-D-ala peptidase, DdpX (VanX, YddT).
3.A.1.5.38.description: The putative D-alanyl-D-alanyl dipeptide permease, DdpABCDF; encoded within an operon that includes the D-ala-D-ala peptidase, DdpX (VanX, YddT). May also interact with the YegQ peptidase (P76403).

3.A.1.5.39.name: Di- and tri-peptide transporter, DppBCDF with periplasmic substrate binding receptors, A1, A3, A5, A7 and A9, each with differing specificities for…
3.A.1.5.39.description: Di- and tri-peptide transporter, DppBCDF with periplasmic substrate binding receptors, A1, A3, A5, A7 and A9, each with differing specificities for peptides ( Pletzer et al. 2014 ).

3.A.1.5.40.name: Nickel uptake porter, NikAB(CD)E.
3.A.1.5.40.description: Nickel uptake porter, NikAB(CD)E ( Benoit et al. 2013 ).

3.A.1.5.41.name: Oligopeptide transporter, OppABCDF/MppA/YgiS.
3.A.1.5.41.description: Oligopeptide transporter, OppABCDF/MppA/YgiS. MppA is a murein peptide receptor, and YgiS is a bile acid (e.g., cholate, deoxycholate) receptor that may use the Opp system for uptake. YgiS mRNA is degraded by the toxin, MgsR, which is regulated by the antitoxin, MgsA, and this loss of the mRNA protects the cell against bile acid stress ( Kwan et al. 2015 ). oppA translation is activated by MicF…

3.A.1.5.42.name: Peptide transporter, SapABCDF.
3.A.1.5.42.description: Peptide transporter, SapABCDF. The Sap transport system renders resistance against host-produced antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) amongst various Gram-negative bacteria ( Dasgupta and Kanaujia 2025 ). The Sap system imports the AMPs across the membrane into the cytoplasm, wherein they are cleaved by proteases. The membrane components (SapBCDF) may also function as a putrescine exporter. Its…

3.A.1.5.43.name: The metal-staphylopine (nicotianamine-like metalophore) complex uptake system, CntABCDF.
3.A.1.5.43.description: The metal-staphylopine (nicotianamine-like metalophore) complex uptake system, CntABCDF. Staphylopine binds divalent nickel, cobalt, zinc, copper and iron ( Ghssein et al. 2016 ).

3.A.1.5.44.name: Peptide transporter, SapABCDF.
3.A.1.5.44.description: Peptide transporter, SapABCDF. Mutants are more sensitive than the wild type to wheat alpha-thionin and to snakin-1, which is the most abundant antimicrobial peptide from potato tubers. They were also less virulent than was the wild-type strain in potato tubers: lesion areas were 37% that of the control, and the growth rate was two orders of magnitude lower. Thus, the interaction of antimicrobial…

3.A.1.5.48.name: Putative peptide uptake porter, DppABCD where A is a periplasmic receptor (R) B and C are membrane proteins (M) and D is a cytoplasmic ATPase (C).
3.A.1.5.48.description: Putative peptide uptake porter, DppABCD where A is a periplasmic receptor (R) B and C are membrane proteins (M) and D is a cytoplasmic ATPase (C) ( Mandal et al. 2021 ).

3.A.1.5.49.name: YejABEF with four subunits as indicated with YejA, a periplasmic peptide binding protein of 610 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS, YejB, a membrane protein…
3.A.1.5.49.description: YejABEF with four subunits as indicated with YejA, a periplasmic peptide binding protein of 610 aas and 1 N-terminal TMS, YejB, a membrane protein with 360 aas and 6 TMSs, YejE, a membrane protein with 377 aas and 6 TMSs, and YejF, and an ATPase with 542 aas.

3.A.1.5.5.name: Probable cationic peptide porter (may also take up peptide antibiotics and protamine; implicated in K + homeostasis) [SapD can stimulate the K +…
3.A.1.5.5.description: Probable cationic peptide porter (may also take up peptide antibiotics and protamine; implicated in K + homeostasis) [SapD can stimulate the K + uptake activities of TrkH and TrkG (TC #2.A.38.1.1) in the presence of ATP] ( Mason et al ., 2006 )

3.A.1.5.50.name: Peptide transporter, OppABCD of 591, 325, 291 and 612 aas with 1, 6, 6, and 0 TMSs, respectively.
3.A.1.5.50.description: Peptide transporter, OppABCD of 591, 325, 291 and 612 aas with 1, 6, 6, and 0 TMSs, respectively. The high-resolution structures of Mycobacterium tuberculosis OppABCD in the resting state, oligopeptide-bound pre-translocation state, AMPPNP-bound pre-catalytic intermediate state and ATP-bound catalytic intermediate state has been obtained. The structures show an assembly of a cluster C SBP with…

3.A.1.5.6.name: The β-glucoside (cellobiose (β-1,4), cellotriose, cellotetraose, cellopentaose, laminaribiose (β-1,3), laminaritriose, sophorose) uptake porter…
3.A.1.5.6.description: The β-glucoside (cellobiose (β-1,4), cellotriose, cellotetraose, cellopentaose, laminaribiose (β-1,3), laminaritriose, sophorose) uptake porter, CbtABCDF

3.A.1.5.7.description: The α-galactoside (melibiose, raffinose) uptake porter, AgpABCDF

3.A.1.6.10.name: Tungstate uptake porter with three subunits, R, M and C.
3.A.1.6.10.description: Tungstate uptake porter with three subunits, R, M and C ( Mandal et al. 2019 ).

3.A.1.6.11.description: High affinity tungstate-specific uptake porter (Km = 1 pM) ( Smart et al. 2009 ).

The unphosphorylated EIIA Ntr protein of the PTS (TC# 4.A) activates PhoR, the senor kinase that phosphorylates the response regulator, PhoB, that activates the pho regulon ( Lüttmann et al. 2012 ).

3.A.1.8.1.description: Molybdate porter consisting of three proteins. Molybdate, after transport into cells by the ModABC proteins, is metabolized by the products of the mol gene(s) ( Maupin-Furlow et al. 1995 ). The repressor of the mod operon is ModE ( Grunden et al. 1996 ).

3.A.1.9.1.description: Phosphonate/organophosphate ester porter (broad specificity). Reviewed by Hinz & Tampé ( 2012 ).

3.A.15.2.1.description: The pilin secretion/fimbrial assembly system. The PilB and PilT ATPases act antagonistically in Type IV pilus function in Myxococcus xanthus . ATP binding and hydrolysis by PilT are essential for T4P extension while ATP binding and hydrolysis by PilB are essential for T4P retraction.
